ideas.title: Condition-transfer estimand E-CT: same-lab, same-extractant mean-sibling template with sibling-count shrinkage, a 0-4 read ladder, a harm rule and publication-unit inference
ideas.fate: Run now as the frozen, separately registered estimand E-CT. Absorbs M02 (read-ladder row), M03 (weighting factorial), M04 (reference-condition line), M06 annex; M05 is its prospective external leg.

J1_information.reason: Only lever above 0.50 at k=3; skeptic fixes add information (offsets capture about 95 % of the gain, survives V2 cleaning, SH helps with one sibling); external leg data-gated.

J2_practical.reason: Most practical value: a direct rule (shrunk own-series mean plus 2-4 reads); gain survives cleaning; needs the offset comparator and same-campaign wording.

J3_feasibility.reason: Training-free, hours; dev legs settle nothing but the open contrasts (SH vs OFF, subsampling, V2-clean, Ce/Gd decomposition) carry decision content.

prior.note: About 0.5 that it holds externally for DGA-type dense-grid labs; template-specific part (beating OFF) about 0.3.

key_fixes: V2-clean primary population from metadata only (drop round-3 D1-D3 duplicates as targets and siblings; drop siblings differing only in contact time or metal concentration); shape-sd rule as sensitivity. V2-clean n_sib>=2 without C5-BTBP: 99 cells, B1 0.531 -> SH 0.707.

Add the cheapest same-information comparator: extractant x publication pair-type offsets of B1's residual, leave-one-cell-out, K pinned: 0.665-0.673 vs SH 0.682 (about 95 % of the gain). Narrow the template claim if SH - OFF < +0.01 R2.

Within-publication sibling subsampling m = 1, 2, 3, 5: SH 0.416/0.454/0.473/0.504/0.531 vs B1 0.352; raw template 0.11 -> 0.52. SH helps with one sibling (n_sib = 1: 0.601 vs 0.544); correct the hypothesis and budget rule.
Publication x chemotype as unit with chemotype-stratified sign-flip and LOPO jackknife (3 clusters, cluster inference impossible); top-3 share 74 %, 13/14 units positive.
Separate same-campaign from same-laboratory (annotate labs from DOIs); report gain by pair type: Ce pairs 32 %, Gd pairs 28 %.
verdicts.notes_summary: Reproduced E6 exactly (SIB 0.5734, SH 0.5946, B1 0.4489, 1,111 rows, 149 cells). Core template not new (E6 6.8, H-SIBLING); the contribution is the G2 test design. Kills (a)-(c) pass on seen data; leg (e) is the real test and is data-gated.

fatal_flaws: Development kills (a)-(c) cannot fail: stratum (a) SH - B1 +0.172, leave-one-family-out lower bound +0.089; the dev run re-describes seen cells.
Only real kill (e) is data-gated and underpowered: per-family gain sd 0.12-0.14; with 5 families the +0.03 rule passes about 0.30 of the time at zero effect and kills a +0.05 effect 36 % of the time.
Decisive stratum is essentially one DGA cluster: 82.6 % of rows in g:pub_74428aeab2, cluster Kish about 1.4; outside it only 5 cells.

key_fixes: Frozen descriptive registration; (a)-(c) become consistency checks; the kill rests on prospective data.
Size the external test in laboratory units: +0.10 needs about 11-14 independent lab x extractant families with >= 3 conditions; +0.05 about 40.
Combined data request: 3 conditions per new lab x chemotype (one cell for BP/BPG confirmation, two as siblings).
At 2-3 reads shrink toward B1 or PWL fitted on the same reads (SH@2 borrows 4-read B1).

Condition-change strata from cond__ metadata (mixed siblings carry 83-93 % of the gain); exclude contact-time-only siblings (SIB R2 1.000 in 6 cells); placebo blends at the same w; lead with the 0-read result (copy 0.436-0.471 vs B1 0.470-0.510).

idea.title: Condition-transfer estimand E-CT: same-lab, same-extractant mean-sibling template with sibling-count shrinkage, a 0-4 read ladder, a harm rule and publication-unit inference
idea.lens: regime / estimand reframing (known laboratory and extractant, new condition) + evaluation unit design
idea.hypothesis: When a laboratory already has at least 2 full series of the same extractant at other conditions, the mean-sibling template plus PWL_R of the read residuals, shrunk toward B1 by w = n/(n+K), predicts strict-adjacent log SF at the new condition clearly better than B1 at 4 reads (>= +0.05 R2 without C5-BTBP and near-copies). With only one prior series there is no gain. The gain is consistent across publications but not yet across source clusters.
idea.rationale: The systematic remainder after B1 is source-local (roughness r +0.36 within publication x extractant, about 0 across publications), so BP/BPG removes it by construction. H-SIBLING is ranked first in the evidence base, but gap G2 is open: no combination rule, no sibling-count dependence, no k ladder, no unit of inference. The knowledge state matches a real question (I ran this extractant before; how few metals at the new acidity?). It must be registered as its own estimand.
idea.evidence_for:
Exploratory, BPG, 5 seeds, E6 rows (1,111 rows/seed, 149 cells, 19 publications), E6 reproduced exactly.
- Mean template 0.573, shrunk (K=2) 0.594 vs B1 0.449.
- Read ladder 0/2/3/4 reads: 0.411 / 0.517 / 0.554 / 0.573 vs D7 - / 0.193 / 0.403 / 0.447.
- n_sib >= 2, no C5-BTBP (112 cells): 0.675 / 0.682 vs B1 0.510; 2 reads 0.595.
- Leave-one-publication-out gain +0.125 (se 0.044, min +0.100); 14/19 publications improve; publication sign test p 0.032, IM-t p 0.001.
- Laboratory-specific: other-publication same-extractant template 0.401 vs 0.386; other-extractant same-publication template 0.336 vs 0.476.
- Mean of all siblings beats nearest-condition sibling (0.573 vs 0.537).
idea.evidence_against:
- Gain is an averaging effect: a single random sibling scores 0.290 (worse than B1); n_sib = 1 stratum 0.513 vs B1 0.544.
- Three publications carry about 86 % of the gain (C5-BTBP about 42 %, whose siblings share a suspected floor); positive-gain Kish 4.5.
- By cluster only 4 wins / 3 losses (sign-flip p 0.18); three small single-publication clusters with 1-2 siblings lose 26-37 % SSE.
- Outside the giant cluster without C5-BTBP raw SIB loses (0.440 vs 0.470); only the shrunk version wins (0.536).
- Near-copies (shape sd < 0.02; 47/149 cells) inflate win counts. K = 2 and the stratum cut were chosen after seeing rows; the two source analyses disagree on the cut (>= 2 vs >= 3 siblings).
idea.test_design:
1. Register E-CT separately; never compared with or substituted for the BP/BPG 0.452.
2. Population: C3 cells with >= 1 same-publication, same-extractant cell covering the target metals (metadata only). Hold out one condition at a time.
3. Pre-declared strata: n_sib = 1, 2, >= 3 (2-7 and >= 8 as sensitivity).
4. Reads: DOPT_Q nested sets at 0, 2, 3, 4 reads on rows identical to REF.
5. Frozen predictor: T = mean sibling curve; SIB = T + PWL_R(y_S - T_S) along -r(CN8); SH = w*SIB + (1-w)*B1 with w = n/(n+2); variant K chosen leave-one-publication-out.
6. Baselines on identical rows: B1 at same k and at 4 reads, copy-mean (0 reads), nearest-condition sibling, random single sibling (exact expectation), publication x pair offsets (nested K).
7. Controls: same-extractant other-publication template; other-extractant same-publication template; near-copy and SF-twin exclusion; without C5-BTBP; inside |predicted level| <= 2.
8. Inference: unit = publication x extractant; IM-t with the size correction from M36 (or a chemotype-stratified permutation), cluster sign-flip as reported sensitivity; per-publication relative SSE and top-3 share.
9. Harm rule: in the 1-2-sibling stratum SH may not be worse than B1 by > 5 % relative SSE, else the deployed rule depends on sibling count.
10. Secondary: lab-conditional conformal 80 % intervals. Confirmation on new multi-condition publications after freezing (M05).
idea.kill_criterion: Claim abandoned if any holds: (a) n_sib >= 2, no C5-BTBP, no near-copies: SH(4 reads) - B1(4 reads) < +0.05 R2 or publication-jackknife 95 % lower bound <= 0; (b) SH with 2 reads < 0.50 in that stratum; (c) the other-publication template reaches >= 70 % of the gain on overlapping rows; (e) on >= 5 new publications SH - B1 < +0.03. If only the equal-weight gain outside the giant cluster is <= 0, narrow the claim to DGA-type labs with dense condition grids. No gain at n_sib = 1 restricts the claim ('needs >= 2 prior series'); it does not kill it.
idea.expected_effect: n_sib >= 2 without C5-BTBP: about 0.65-0.68 at 4 reads vs B1 about 0.51; about 0.57-0.60 at 2 reads (above B1 with 4 reads and no history). n_sib = 1: about 0. Equal-cluster gain much smaller than pooled (about +7 % vs +23 % SSE). On new data expect +0.05 to +0.10.
idea.practical_value: A budget rule for a chemist: with >= 2 prior own series of the extractant, measure 2 metals at the new condition and use the mean of the old series as template; with one prior series use B1 with 4 metals; curves of the same extractant from other laboratories are not a substitute. Turns a condition scan into full series at 2-3 anchor conditions plus 2 metals elsewhere.
idea.risks: Same-paper shared artefacts (floor, calibration, re-reports) make the template predict errors; few publications drive the gain; K and strata are post hoc; strong publication dependence; must never be quoted beside 0.452; confirmation needs new multi-condition series the archive lacks.
idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: regime-1, evaluation-5; adds to H-SIBLING / E6 6.8 the 0-4 read ladder, the finding that the gain needs >= 2 siblings (averaging), a sibling-count shrinkage rule that rescues non-giant clusters, a harm rule, and the publication-vs-cluster unit split (14/5 vs 4/3).

ideas.title: Few-cluster-valid paired tests: cluster sign-flip randomisation on (log) SSE ratios and an Ibragimov-Muller t-test, calibrated by a heavy-tailed hierarchical simulator
ideas.fate: Run now as a minutes-long source-level resampling replay; seals unit, test and alpha. Absorbs M36 (unit aggregation) and M37 (ledger behind the M33 gate).

J1_information.reason: Shared inference infrastructure; power is unit-dependent; reframes confirmation planning (13-20 publication-like sources vs 40-80).

J2_practical.reason: Could change the data request (ask for many independent labs); value to a chemist indirect.

J3_feasibility.reason: Runs in minutes on stored OOF as a replay; decides the planning number; no chemistry verdict.

prior.note: About 0.2 that power reaches 0.6 at G = 6-8 for realistic sources; the replay itself is almost certainly informative.

Comparator is a straw man (sealed triple with Kish floor and MAE leg); most power from switching estimand; HBK@ML-B0 equal-weight p 0.01-0.02 vs pooled +0.0014.
Generator calibrated to row residual moments, not between-source contrast moments; about 10 targets each in a 90 % band pass a correct generator only about 35 % of the time.

Compare against WCR + CR2 and Kish-df jackknife-t on the same estimand and alpha.
Exact one-sided binomial sign test for 'helped in most sources'; skewed nulls with >= 2,000 reps; Clopper-Pearson kill.
One-sided 0.05; G >= 6 floor; seal unit, test and tie rule before any round-5 contrast; merge with M35 and M36.

fatal_flaws: Power claim holds only for cpg-like aggregate sources: G = 8 one-sided 0.025/0.05: cpg 0.55-0.68/0.69-0.84; publication 0.30-0.35/0.39-0.52; chemotype about 0.22/0.30-0.36; inside the giant DGA cluster per-chemotype B1-B0 mean log ratio -0.056.
Size kill is a choice of world: skewed real per-unit nulls give 0.16-0.35 in one tail.
Alpha mismatch: sealed rule is one-sided 0.025; G = 5 cannot reject at 0.025.
IM-t on relative SSE unstable across units (t +2.65 cpg vs -0.71 chemotype).
key_fixes: Replace the days-long generator with a source-level resampling replay of per-unit statistics from stored OOF at three granularities, tau in {0, 0.065} (minutes).
One-sided 0.025 primary; compare against the sealed R2 leg alone on the same draws.
Estimand pi with an exact binomial sign test plus a pooled-ratio magnitude guard; register it as a separate estimand E-S.
Parameterise effects by consistency; declare the unit before data; kill: power < 0.30 at G = 8 with publication units keeps the 40-80 planning number.
verdicts.notes_summary: Could cut the planning number to about 13-20 publication-sized sources for consistent effects; shared infrastructure for M35-M37; no round-4 verdict changes.

idea.title: Few-cluster-valid paired tests: cluster sign-flip randomisation on (log) SSE ratios and an Ibragimov-Muller t-test, calibrated by a heavy-tailed hierarchical simulator
idea.lens: evaluation and inference design (few large heterogeneous clusters)
idea.hypothesis: With 13 clusters (Kish 2.24), a cluster sign-flip randomisation test (pooled dSSE or the mean per-cluster log SSE ratio) and an IM t-test across per-cluster relative SSE keep size <= 0.05-0.075 under calibrated nulls and have clearly more power than the sealed percentile/BCa/jackknife triple, reaching >= 0.6 power at 6-8 new sources for a B1-sized consistent effect.
idea.rationale: The sealed rule is both anti-conservative (5-8 % vs nominal 2.5 % under the boundary null) and powerless (B1 - B0 jackknife interval includes 0). Tests built for few large clusters count the giant cluster once; the log SSE ratio is antisymmetric under arm swap, which is the symmetry the sign-flip test needs, and its smallest p is 2^-G without asymptotics in G.
idea.evidence_for: B1 - B0: 11 of 12 non-tied clusters better; pooled sign-flip p 0.0032 (exact); equal-weight sign-flip p 0.014; mean log SSE ratio +0.160, sign-flip p 0.007 (BPG and BP); IM t 2.60, p 0.012; publication level 31/38, p 0.0001. Every round-4 slot stays null (p >= 0.12); S02's pooled loss is a big-fold effect (+0.017 on the balanced metric). Smallest attainable p 0.031 at G = 5, 0.016 at G = 6.
idea.evidence_against: B1 - B0 on development data checks sensitivity, not confirmation; exactness needs independent clusters and sign symmetry; pooled sign-flip inherits giant-cluster dominance (one cluster holds 83-86 % of |dSSE| for S02, S06); HBK@ML - B0 rejects under equal weighting (p 0.017) but not pooled (0.46), which is either a real small-cluster gain or a false positive; tiny clusters make relative SSE heavy-tailed; the round-4 generator was miscalibrated (S05 and S11 gained +0.02 in null worlds).
idea.test_design: (1) One generator built from B1's real OOF residuals: per-cell offset (36 % of pointwise energy), AR(1) drift along hidden runs (rho 0.69), metal-specific Student-t spikes, publication x pair effects, same-extractant cross-publication correlation 0.10-0.14, cluster heterogeneity tau 0.065. Calibrate to kurtosis 18.2, top 1 % / 5 % SSE shares 31 % / 59 %, lag-1 / lag-2 pair correlations -0.522 / +0.091, the K curve of publication offsets, per-cluster SSE shares and the real per-cluster dSSE spread of near-null contrasts; accept only if every target lies in its bootstrap 90 % band. (2) Worlds: exchangeable null; heterogeneous zero-mean null (small-cluster gains, equal giant-cluster loss); SSE-preserving boundary null; effects delta = 0.01 / 0.02 / 0.034, homogeneous and heterogeneous; >= 200 replicates; development geometry and new-source sets G = 5, 8, 10, 13, 20, 40. (3) Tests: sealed rule (control), pooled and equal-weight cluster sign-flip, sign-flip on mean log SSE ratio and a studentised version, publication sign-flip, IM-t on relative SSE and on log ratio, jackknife-t with Kish df, CR2 with Bell-McCaffrey df, wild cluster restricted bootstrap with Webb weights. (4) Before any round-5 contrast is scored, declare one test per estimand (pooled -> sign-flip; equal-weight -> IM-t) with balanced MAE as a non-inferiority guard.
idea.kill_criterion: A test is dropped if its size exceeds 0.075 at nominal 0.05 in any calibrated null world (heterogeneous null included), or its power at delta = 0.034, G = 20 is not >= the sealed rule's + 0.10. If the sign-flip test has power < 0.3 at G = 8 for a B1-sized effect, keep POWER.md's 40-80-source conclusion and treat round-5 model contrasts as diagnostics.
idea.expected_effect: Nominal size and about 2-3x the sealed rule's power for consistent effects; power 0.5-0.8 at G = 6-8 for a B1-sized effect; < 0.2 for +0.01 effects; no round-4 verdict changes.
idea.practical_value: 'Did the Gd correction help in most independent sources?' becomes testable: development evidence now, confirmation with about 6-20 new sources instead of 40-80.
idea.risks: Equal weighting answers 'the average source', not 'the average row', and must never replace pooled R2; simulator misspecification; clusters not fully independent (copy groups, shared labs); the choice must be sealed before new data.
idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: evaluation-1, statistics-4; first few-cluster-valid tests computed on this corpus, a residual-calibrated generator (gap G7), and a balanced re-scoring of round-4 slots (gap G4).

ideas.title: One currency for decisions: pooled and equal-weight relative pair-SSE vs B1 as co-primary, balanced-MAE guard, BPG deciding, mandatory per-cluster and fold-type tables, replayed on all stored arms
ideas.fate: Seal now as a protocol amendment (relative-SSE gate, balanced-MAE guard, BPG decides, mandatory tables). Absorbs M38's retire-only gate, M21's provenance column, M08's moment table.

J1_information.reason: Worth sealing; equal-weight IM-t leg flawed (blind to giant-cluster gains, tiny-cluster votes, Holm kills positive control).

J2_practical.reason: Cheap protocol hygiene; minimal chemist value.

J3_feasibility.reason: Cheap prerequisite for coherent round-5 decisions; equal-weight gate unvalidated.

prior.note: Convention sound; the 1.3x signal-to-noise claim is circular.

fatal_flaws: As written, Holm over the 14-contrast replay family gives B1-B0 IM-t p 0.0117 -> 0.164, killing the positive control.
Replay cannot discriminate rules: the sealed round-4 rule also passes B1-B0 and rejects the same arms.
1.5x signal-to-noise is a ratio of two t statistics on one contrast chosen among five statistics (circular).
Equal-weight IM-t has zero power for a gain confined to the giant cluster (t = 1 exactly); 8 of 13 weights go to 1-4-cell single-publication clusters (mostly ORNL-only).
HBK@ML lead is double dipping (signal from 8 tiny clusters).
key_fixes: B1-B0 as single positive control, unadjusted; Holm only inside the round-5 decision family.
Compare whole-rule power and size in M34's generator under four effect geometries; demote the equal-weight leg if false-pass > 0.05 or giant-only power < 0.2.
Pool tiny clusters; log SSE ratio for IM-t; publication-level diagnostic inside the giant cluster.
Drop the HBK@ML E-B lead; restrict the six-design table to training-free arms; seal with M34 and M38.
verdicts.notes_summary: Replay reproduces (B1-B0 pooled +5.85 %, equal-weight +12.3 %, log ratio +14.75 %). Survives as a sealed reporting and decision convention, not an empirical hypothesis.

fatal_flaws: Kill criteria not real tests: replay outcome known; Holm kills the positive control; SNR criterion circular (equal-weight/delta-R2 t ratio 1.50 B1, 13 S02, 31 HBK@ML).
Equal-weight leg cannot tell B1-B0 (sign-flip p 0.0137) from FIRM-null HBK@ML-B0 (p 0.0115).
Weighting population: 62 % of votes to clusters holding 6.4 % of rows; cluster_cpg is not 'the average laboratory'; a 10 % giant-only SSE cut fails the IM-t.
Proposed lead test already computed (HBK+Gd vs B1: pooled -0.35 %, equal-weight +8.3 %, p 0.014).
Low decision value: no round-4 verdict changes.
key_fixes: Seal: E-A continuity; pooled relative SSE >= 2 % gate; balanced-MAE guard >= -0.001; BPG decides; per-cluster, per-fold and six-design tables.
Equal-weight leg as a breadth diagnostic unless calibrated in M34 (size <= 0.05-0.075 and power >= 0.5 for homogeneous 2 %).
Pool clusters < 5 cells or < 30 rows; provenance sensitivity with ORNL-only clusters pooled.
Record HBK@ML+Gd only as a hypothesis for new sources.
verdicts.notes_summary: IM-t power for a homogeneous 2 % effect: 0.96 at nuisance sd 0.02, 0.39 at 0.05, 0.21 at 0.08.

idea.title: One currency for decisions: pooled and equal-weight relative pair-SSE vs B1 as co-primary, balanced-MAE guard, BPG deciding, mandatory per-cluster and fold-type tables, replayed on all stored arms
idea.lens: evaluation design (decision metric and margins)
idea.hypothesis: A decision rule written entirely in relative pair-SSE vs B1 (pooled reduction >= 2 %; equal-weight cluster mean > 0 by IM-t; balanced MAE change >= -0.001) passes the one known positive (B1 vs B0), rejects every round-4 loser, and has about 1.5x the signal-to-noise of delta R2 with a 0.005 balanced-MAE margin. Where the two weightings disagree, the result is a lead, not a claim.
idea.rationale: The current margins are in different currencies (0.005 balanced MAE is about +0.034-0.053 R2; block A's MAE leg was unreachable even as an oracle), pooled R2 weights the giant cluster at 0.65, and the deciding fold trains on 51-69 cells. Relative SSE vs B1 is one currency (2 % about +0.011 R2 about 0.0015 balanced MAE) with a pooled and an equal-cluster form.
idea.evidence_for: B1 - B0 under each statistic (cluster-jackknife t): delta R2 +0.034 (1.73); relative SSE pooled +5.9 % (1.99); sqrt(n)-weighted +9.3 % (2.55); equal-weight +12.4 % (2.60); log ratio +15.1 % (2.89). Replay: B1 - B0 passes all three legs (5.9 %, IM p 0.012, +0.005 MAE); every other arm fails the pooled leg (S01 -0.02 %, S02 -4.4 %, S05 -1.1 %, S06 -1.0 %, S11 -0.1 %, B2 -4.0 %, HIST_D7 -0.2 %). In the non-big folds no round-4 slot reaches 2 % either, so the big fold hid no gain.
idea.evidence_against: The weighting changes conclusions: S02 is -4.4 % pooled but +1.0-1.5 % equal-weight (9 of 13 clusters better, IM p 0.24); HBK@ML - B0 is +0.13 % pooled but +7 % equal-weight (IM p 0.017), contradicting the FIRM 'learned curve models <= PWL' under that weighting, though it fails Holm over about 15 contrasts; equal weighting gives 1-2-cell clusters the voice of the 162-cell cluster.
idea.test_design: 1. Seal before any round-5 score: E-A pooled R2 (continuity); co-primary relative pair-SSE vs B1, pooled (margin >= 2 %) and equal-weight cluster mean (IM-t, one-sided 0.05; test choice from M34); guard balanced MAE change >= -0.001; BPG decides and BP is a labelled sensitivity; mandatory per-cluster (13 rows), per-fold-type and six-design diagnostic tables. 2. Retrospective replay (minutes) with Holm on stored OOF predictions of REF, S01, S02, S05, S06, S11, R3-R02, R3-R14, LINE, RIDGE2, HBK@ML, G14@ZERO, B2, HIST_D7: must pass B1 - B0 and reject every round-4 slot. 3. Disagreement rule: one weighting negative and the other significant -> a weighting-dependent lead registered as an E-B contrast; first candidate HBK@ML base plus a fold-fitted Gd amplitude vs B1, reported per cluster.
idea.kill_criterion: Co-primary abandoned if the replay fails B1 - B0 or passes any round-4 slot, or if in calibrated synthetic worlds (M34) the equal-weight signal-to-noise for a B1-like effect is not >= 1.3x that of delta R2. The HBK@ML lead is dropped if its E-B contrast vs B1 is <= 0 or has IM p > 0.05.
idea.expected_effect: The 0.452 reference is unchanged; margin legs become consistent; about 1.5x signal-to-noise for consistent effects; a written rule for disagreements.
idea.practical_value: One number with two readings: how much a method helps the average pair, and whether it helps the average independent laboratory; if the HBK@ML flag is real, learned curve models help small unusual sources while tying on the DGA-dominated pool.
idea.risks: The equal-weight leg invites cherry-picking unless sealed first; tiny clusters flip signs by noise; changing currency breaks comparability unless E-A stays reported.
idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: evaluation-2; the signal-to-noise table, the replay against every stored arm, the S02 and HBK@ML weighting flips, and the check that per-fold-type reporting would not have changed any round-4 verdict.

idea.title: Gate floor-aware predictors on a source-stated detection limit: the clamp's sign flips within 0.5 log of its threshold
idea.lens: data quality (decidability gate)
idea.hypothesis: A reads-only floor-aware predictor cannot be validated on V1: its effect depends so steeply on the floor threshold F that any F chosen on V1 is fitted to the C5-BTBP cells' labels. Only a source-stated detection limit can fix F.
idea.rationale: The floor-aware predictor is listed as runnable in software; if its outcome is decided by a free threshold, a round-5 slot would spend power on a knife-edge or invite post hoc threshold choice. A cheap diagnostic closes or gates it first.
idea.evidence_for: Read clamp (reads below F set to F) added to B1, BPG (BP identical to 3 decimals): F = -4.5 0.464; -4.25 0.471; -4.0 0.458; -3.75 0.411; -3.5 0.317; -3.0 -0.079 (B1 0.452). Prediction clamp at -4.25: 0.470. For F <= -4 SSE changes only on C5-BTBP rows; at -3.5 those rows lose +12.1 SSE/seed. The good window is about 0.5 log wide and sits at the cells' own floor value.
idea.evidence_against: If the closed papers state a limit near -4.3, the predictor would give a real but source-local +0.01 to +0.02; the clamp is one of several censored forms (a smoother Tobit-type interpolation was not tried).
idea.test_design: 1. Pre-register now: no floor-aware predictor is a round-5 decision slot unless F comes from a source document (experimental sections of the candidate source papers, or a lab's stated per-metal limit); record the exploratory F-curve as already seen. 2. When F_src arrives: run both clamps at F_src on V1 C3 k = 3 DOPT_Q, BPG deciding; report C5-BTBP rows and other rows separately; robustness band F_src +/- 0.25; control: the same clamp on a label-free random 15-cell subset of non-floor cells. 3. Any Tobit-type variant pre-specified with the same band.
idea.kill_criterion: Floor-aware predictors retired (floors kept only in scoring, M23) if at F_src the gain vs B1 < +0.005 R2, or its sign flips anywhere in F_src +/- 0.25, or the gain comes only from pub_6a0ef8528c (then it counts as a source-local data fix, not a model claim).
idea.expected_effect: None now (the output is a gate). With a source limit near -4.25 to -4.5, a source-local +0.01 to +0.02; with a limit at or above -3.75 the predictor would be harmful.
idea.practical_value: A generic 'clamp below-detection values' rule is dangerous unless the limit is known to about 0.25 log; laboratories should report per-metal detection limits or '< DL' rather than a number; no software effort on floor modelling before the source arrives.
idea.risks: 'Retired' could be misread as 'floor absent' (it means undecidable without the limit); the decisive run needs the user's journal access.
idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: data_quality-3; first measurement of the floor predictor's threshold dependence, turning it from a candidate slot into a gate on source evidence.

idea.title: Known-extractant estimand: transfer only the f-shell anomalies (Gd, and Nd for DGAs) from other publications
idea.lens: physics and chemistry (condition-invariant f-shell anomalies) + publication hold-out
idea.hypothesis: For an extractant or chemotype documented in other publications, transferring only its Gd dip and (for DGAs) its Nd dip, shrunk toward B1, beats B1 and the full cross-publication template on held-out publications; adding Ce or all metals makes it worse, because only these anomalies are reproducible chemistry.
idea.rationale: The Gd dip has ICC 0.69 by extractant and does not move with acid within an extractant; the sc009 Nd dip appears in every sc009 publication; whole-curve copies across publications fail. A 2-number transfer is a physics-constrained, low-variance alternative to 14-offset corrections that failed under publication hold-out.
idea.evidence_for: sc009 Nd chord negative in every publication (-0.04 to -0.22) vs +0.004 elsewhere. sc009 Nd potential chosen leave-one-publication-out: +0.0063 (5/5 seeds); sc009 Pr/Nd 0.26 -> 0.53. Same extractant, other publication (786 rows/seed): B1 0.386; Gd only 0.409; Gd+Nd 0.427; Gd+Nd+Ce 0.421; full template 0.401. Within publication about 45 % of the sibling gain is carried by three metal anomalies.

idea.test_design: Separate estimand E-KX: held-out-publication cells under BP folds whose extractant (Gd) or chemotype (Nd) has training cells in other publications. Pre-declared exclusions: copy groups and the suspected C5-BTBP duplicate pair; report with and without C5-BTBP. B1-KX: u_Gd(extractant) and u_Nd(chemotype) = training-publication mean chord anomaly, shrunk n/(n+5) toward B1's beta and 0, entered as point potentials (reads stay exact); unseen extractants fall back to B1. Controls: B1; full cross-publication template; anomalies from a random other extractant of the same family (200 draws); +Ce variant; all-12-metal variant. Endpoints: pooled R2, Pr/Nd and Gd-pair R2, per-publication contrasts, balanced MAE.
idea.kill_criterion: On E-KX rows without C5-BTBP: gain < +0.005, or < 4/5 seeds positive, or the random-extractant permutation reaches the observed gain, or the +Ce or all-metal variant does as well or better.
idea.expected_effect: +0.005 to +0.01 without C5-BTBP; sc009 Pr/Nd from about 0.26 to about 0.5.
idea.practical_value: A chemist using a literature extractant under new conditions can borrow two numbers (its Gd dip and, for DGAs, its Nd dip) and improve Pr/Nd and Gd-region SF estimates; a Pr/Nd SF from plain DGA radius interpolation is too optimistic (matters for magnet-metal separation); do not borrow Ce or other roughness from other labs.

idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: physics-2; first anomaly-only transfer by extractant under publication hold-out, and the decomposition showing Ce does not transfer while Gd and Nd do.

idea.title: Sibling weighting rule head-to-head: condition-kernel empirical-Bayes BLUP vs read-level matching vs the plain mean template
idea.lens: statistical modelling of laboratory random effects (EB shrinkage, condition kernel) vs label-free level matching
idea.hypothesis: How siblings are weighted matters. Either (a) an empirical-Bayes BLUP of B1 residuals from siblings, weighted by an acid-distance kernel and shrunk by sibling count (two levels: same extractant; other extractant of the same publication), or (b) averaging the two siblings whose levels at the 4 reads are closest (label-free), beats the unweighted mean template and B1 on identical rows. A level-farthest or random single sibling is worse than B1, and per-metal extrapolation of acid trends fails.
idea.rationale: Gap G2 asks how to combine several siblings and how condition distance matters. The two candidate answers point to different distance axes (acid distance vs read-level distance), so they are competitors and should be scored head-to-head inside one registration rather than as separate claims.
idea.evidence_for:
(a) Kernel BLUP (nested hyperparameters, leave-publication-out scalars): all C3 rows 0.564 vs B1 0.452; rows with a same-extractant sibling 0.626 vs unshrunk template 0.567; without C5-BTBP 0.571; outside the big cluster 0.567; near-identical siblings dropped 0.546. Single-sibling residual correlation decays with |dlog acid| (0.60 up to 0.2; 0.14 at 0.5-1; 0.04 above 1). Shrinkage slope 0.30 for one sibling vs 0.74-0.91 for >= 2. Read ladder 0/2/3/4: 0.312 / 0.465 / 0.535 / 0.567.
(b) 127 cells with >= 2 siblings: mean of 2 level-nearest 0.620, mean all 0.577, level-nearest 0.537, condition-nearest 0.511, random single 0.225, level-farthest -0.864, B1 0.415 (without C5-BTBP 0.695 / 0.675 / 0.646 / 0.569 / - / - / 0.510). Acid-trend extrapolation -0.064. Diluent-only siblings copy MSE 0.0086 vs acid-only 0.049.
idea.evidence_against:
- Both rule families were designed after seeing these rows.
- Kernel BLUP loses 12.5 % SSE in one cluster and 6-20 % in 4 chemotypes.
- With exactly 3 siblings mean-all beats mean-of-2 (0.775 vs 0.761); level-nearest vs condition-nearest differ by only 0.026, and level and condition distance are confounded.
- About 19 families, dominated by the giant DGA cluster; median-of-siblings gives no robustness gain.
idea.test_design: Inside E-CT (M01), identical rows and reads (ladder at 2, 3, 4 reads). Arms: B1; mean-all template; nearest-condition (pre-declared distance |dlog acid| + |dlog L| + diluent flag); nearest-level; mean of 2 nearest-level; kernel EB BLUP with nested grid ell {0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, inf}, rho {0, 0.3, 0.6}, kappa {0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4}, inner leave-publication-block-out, one-SE rule toward the mean template; publication x pair offsets. Controls: random single (expectation), level-farthest (must be worst), acid values shuffled within publication (tests the kernel), other-publication siblings (negative). Pre-declared near-copy exclusion. Family-cluster bootstrap and leave-one-family-out; report without giant cluster and C5-BTBP; sibling-count x reads subsampling surface. Confirmatory rows only from new families (M05).
idea.kill_criterion: Kernel: nested all-row R2 < 0.52 at 4 reads, or gain over the refitted mean template < +0.01 on covered rows, or the acid-shuffle control within 0.005 (drop the kernel, keep plain EB). Level rule: mean-of-2-level-nearest minus mean-all <= 0 (90 % interval includes -0.01) and level-nearest <= condition-nearest, or level-farthest not the worst arm. If both die, register mean-all only.
idea.expected_effect: +0.01 to +0.06 over the mean template on covered rows; one distance axis likely dominates. All-row R2 about 0.54-0.57 at 4 reads in this regime.
idea.practical_value: Tells a chemist which old series to reuse: matched D level and nearby acidity; average at least two; never extrapolate acid trends metal by metal; diluent swaps preserve adjacent SF better than acid changes.
idea.risks: Post hoc rules; few families; same-paper artefacts; a separate estimand that must not be compared with BP/BPG numbers.
idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: statistics-1, contrarian-2; merges two competing answers to G2 into one crossing, with the sibling-count shrinkage law and the finding that a random single sibling is worse than B1.

idea.title: Registered measurability domain: B1-predicted log D of both metals in [-2, 2], with a nested threshold, composition-matched abstention controls, mechanism checks and window-aware intervals
idea.lens: label-free applicability domain / selective prediction, with a physical a priori threshold
idea.hypothesis: Keeping pairs whose B1-predicted log D of both metals lies in [-2, 2] (declared a priori: one phase holds < 1 % outside it) gives R2 >= 0.50 on >= 70 % of rows, beats random abstention stratified by publication at matched coverage (so it flags rows, not only laboratories), survives leave-one-cluster-out, and leaves an out-of-window error that is unstructured tail noise with no correctable signature.
idea.rationale: The window (0.540 on 74.7 %) beats unstratified random abstention, but the threshold was chosen post hoc, and C5-BTBP is 29 % of out-of-window rows, so part of the gain may be 'drop floor-limited labs'. Composition-matched controls separate the two mechanisms, and fixed mechanism checks decide whether any modelling slot should go to the out-of-window tail.
idea.evidence_for: Threshold curve c = 1 / 1.5 / 2 / 2.5 / 3: coverage 0.455 / 0.603 / 0.747 / 0.847 / 0.927, inside R2 0.571 / 0.557 / 0.540 / 0.501 / 0.495. Nested threshold: 0.544 at 0.672 (coverage >= 0.6) and 0.527 at 0.753 (coverage >= 0.7). LOCO inside 0.505-0.551. MSE inside 0.0189 vs outside about 0.051. Random abstention: unstratified 0.453 [0.436, 0.468]; by pair type 0.4525; by cluster 0.472; by pair type x cluster 0.477; by publication 0.489 [0.473, 0.504], so about +0.036 composition and +0.051 within-publication selection. Within-pair-type R2 0.384 -> 0.480. Robust sd of chord deviations flat across level bins except below -3; no even/odd contamination signature outside C5-BTBP; a minority-phase-concentration window is worse (0.476); lab-shared roughness exists in window only (0.157 vs -0.029).
idea.evidence_against: c = 2 was one of 4 windows tried; per-cluster coverage 0.19 in the BTBP cluster, so part is source exclusion; var(y) inside is lower (0.041 vs 0.049), so report MSE; a cross-fitted heteroscedastic variance model does worse (0.470 at 75 %), a warning that the window may be lucky; out-of-window rows are unbiased (slope 1.013), so there is no point-prediction fix; cleaner new data may shrink the contrast; small publications leave stratified controls little freedom.
idea.test_design: Register E-AD. Grid c in {1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, inf} plus lower-only bounds {-2, -2.5, -3}; primary c = 2 (physical declaration); secondary nested c chosen in training folds (max inside R2 subject to coverage >= 0.7, one-SE toward wider). Arms B0, B1 (fold beta), HIST_D7; BPG decides, BP sensitivity; repeat at k = 4. Report coverage-R2 and coverage-MSE curves, coverage per cluster and pair type, inside/outside MSE ratio per cluster, LOCO, without C5-BTBP; read hull as a second axis. Controls at realised per-unit coverage (1,000 draws each): random, pair-type, cluster, pair type x cluster, publication-stratified. Window-aware Mondrian intervals (pair type x window) vs pair type alone, calibrated leave-one-cluster-out. Mechanism diagnostics with declared sign predictions and publication bootstrap: parity-signed chord vs level; chord sd vs minority-phase concentration; within-publication cross-extractant roughness in vs out. Apply the frozen rule to new sources.
idea.kill_criterion: Killed if: inside R2 at c = 2 < 0.50; or nested inside R2 <= the 97.5 % quantile of the publication-stratified control (then it is a lab/data-quality flag, not a row flag); or LOCO minimum < 0.48; or inside/outside MSE ratio > 0.6 in more than a third of clusters with enough rows on both sides; or window-aware intervals are not >= 15 % narrower inside with per-cluster coverage >= 0.7; or a mechanism diagnostic shows a structured out-of-window signature outside C5-BTBP (tail modellable after all); or on new sources inside R2 < 0.45 or inside MSE not below outside.
idea.expected_effect: Inside R2 about 0.52-0.55 at 67-80 % coverage; +0.03 to +0.05 over the publication-stratified control, about +0.08 over unstratified random; outside about 0.30; intervals roughly 40 % narrower inside. No all-row gain.
idea.practical_value: A rule a chemist applies before trusting a 4-metal estimate: if predicted D of both metals is between 0.01 and 100, the adjacent-SF estimate is at the R2 0.54 / RMSE 0.14 level; otherwise measure the pair or move D into range via acidity, extractant concentration or phase ratio. Also a curation flag.
idea.risks: Threshold history is post hoc; the domain partly encodes 'not C5-BTBP'; inside R2 is not comparable with 0.452 (state coverage); may add nothing on clean new data.
idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: regime-3, statistics-3, physics-4; adds the full threshold curve, nested choice, publication-stratified decomposition, a physical a priori threshold, three mechanism checks already run, and window-aware intervals (gap G6).

idea.title: Figure-versus-table digitisation calibration as a gate: attenuation of single-metal features, digitisation accuracy, then verified figure mining for new independent sources
idea.lens: data quality (measurement-process bias) + LLM-assisted extraction with verification
idea.hypothesis: Re-digitising published figures whose data also exist as tables measures (i) whether digitisation attenuates single-metal features such as the Gd dip (slope < 1) and (ii) the digitisation error of adjacent log SF. If the error sd is <= 0.05 with no material attenuation, double extraction (LLM vision plus a manual digitiser) of the figure-only literature can add >= 30 new independent source clusters and lift confirmation power from <= 0.10 to a usable level.
idea.rationale: FIG cells are markedly smoother with a weaker Gd dip (M21); that is either chemistry or a digitisation artefact, with opposite advice for primary data. Separately, confirmation needs 40-80 new sources while table-based supply is 3-5, and many lanthanide-series papers publish only figures. Both questions are answered by the same calibration experiment, which must pass before figure data are used as reads, labels or confirmation.
idea.evidence_for: FIG vs TAB median |second difference| 0.028 vs 0.049 (within sc009 0.038 vs 0.065); raw Gd dip -0.049 vs -0.093; fitted Gd amplitude -0.040 vs -0.116. In one two-location cell, figure and table differ by -1.10 at La to -0.04 at Gd (light-end-specific). Adjacent-SF disagreement between two data locations of one cell: median 0.025 (two tables), 0.050 (two figures), 0.119 (figure vs table). But by B1 error figure cells are not rougher (MSE 0.016 vs 0.024; within DGA 0.0159 vs 0.0262; publication-level p 0.78), so plotted sources look admissible. Transcription replicate sd 0.049; confirmation power 0.04 / 0.10 / 0.27 at G = 5 / 10 / 40.
idea.evidence_against: FIG cells concentrate in TODGA-type chemistry with a plausibly weak dip; two-location cells are mostly hidden-condition merges; log-axis digitising is usually accurate to 0.01-0.02 decades; an adjacent SF from two digitised points inflates error by sqrt(2); LLM vision can hallucinate coordinates; new figure sources may again be DGA (no Kish gain); copyright and access need the user.
idea.test_design: Phase 1 (user-supplied PDFs; numbers stored, not figures): >= 20 V1 cells whose paper gives the same data as table and figure (corpus papers first; never open-access papers reserved for confirmation). Two independent extractions per figure: LLM vision with calibrated axes and a manual digitiser; reconcile disagreements > 0.05. Metrics vs the table: sd and bias of levels and adjacent log SF, inter-extractor sd, attenuation slope (regression of digitised on table deviations; Gd-dip ratio). In-corpus software part: paired comparison in the 3 FIG+TAB publications and 12 two-location cells (excluding merges) with cell-cluster bootstrap. Pre-declared gate: sd <= 0.05, |bias| <= 0.01, inter-extractor sd <= 0.04, Gd-dip ratio in [0.8, 1.2]. Phase 2: pre-declared open-access full-text search for >= 8-Ln series; yield per 100 papers of independent series, multi-condition families and clusters new to the 13. Phase 3: freeze digitised sources as a sealed confirmation set never used for development.
idea.kill_criterion: Figure route closed if digitisation sd of adjacent log SF > 0.08 (comparable to B1's robust residual sd 0.086) or the search yields < 10 new independent clusters. FIG/TAB difference attributed to chemistry or publication (and provenance-conditional modelling dropped) if re-digitisation repeatability sd <= 0.03 and the figure-vs-table Gd-dip ratio lies in [0.8, 1.2] with a CI excluding 0.6.
idea.expected_effect: Probably accurate enough (sd about 0.03-0.05); +20-60 sources if yield holds, raising confirmation power for a B1-sized effect to about 0.3-0.8; attenuation >= 30 % would justify a primary-data Gd amplitude near -0.10 to -0.12.
idea.practical_value: Tells literature miners whether figure-read values are usable as reads; tells a chemist whether fresh numeric tables need a larger Gd correction than literature curves; is the only realistic route to confirming any claim, and supplies the multi-condition families the within-lab regimes need.
idea.risks: Hallucinated coordinates if verification is skipped; selection bias in which papers have figures; digitiser settings and axis types confound; user effort for access.
idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: data_quality-5, contrarian-7; one shared figure-vs-table calibration serves both the attenuation question and a quantitative accuracy gate for figure mining; neither digitisation attenuation nor figure-only supply had been examined.

idea.title: Metals-to-0.50 on fixed cohorts: the apparent 5-metal crossing on C3 is a cohort-mixture effect
idea.lens: measurement design (k ladder) with like-for-like cohorts
idea.hypothesis: On cells that can actually take extra legal reads, B1 reaches adjacent R2 0.50 only at 6 measured metals (k = 5). The C3 figure of about 0.50 at 5 metals arises because the 51 cells that cannot take a 5th read keep their (easy) k = 3 predictions.
idea.rationale: H-BUDGET ranks second because its estimate sits on 0.50. A C3 ladder row mixes 178 cells scored at k = 4 with 51 cells still at k = 3. The honest 'how many metals' answer must come from fixed cohorts scored at every rung.
idea.evidence_for: C3 with k = min(K, kmax), DOPT_Q / BISECT: K = 4 0.496 / 0.501; K = 5 0.529 / 0.534; K = 6 0.550 / 0.572. Fixed cohorts: C4 K = 3 0.429 / 0.434, K = 4 0.479 / 0.478; C5 K = 4 0.482, K = 5 0.522 / 0.518; C6 K = 5 0.524 / 0.520, K = 6 0.552 / 0.571. The 51 kmax = 3 cells score 0.597 / 0.650 at k = 3 vs 0.429 / 0.434 for kmax >= 4. Consistent with E3 (max-min 5th read 0.503, 3/5 seeds) and E6 (C6 crosses at k = 5).
idea.evidence_against: Beta fixed at -0.072, not refit (gap G3; shift about 0.001-0.005); fixed cohorts are harder than C3, so cohort difficulty and read count are confounded; legality forbids reading a strict neighbour while real labs get measured pairs; BISECT figures come from a policy seen post hoc.
idea.test_design: Registered E-D ladder. Primary: for each K = 1-6 a fixed nested cohort C_K (cells with kmax >= K) scored at every k <= K on identical queries. Secondary: the C3 min(K, kmax) row. Policies DOPT_Q-nested (primary) and BISECT (secondary). Predictors B0, B1 (beta refit per fold and per k, BPG and BP), HIST_D7. Report seed range, cluster bootstrap, LOCO, kmax strata (3, 4-5, 6), balanced MAE, and P(R2 >= 0.50) with interval (M38) rather than pass/fail. Pre-declared k* = smallest K with fixed-cohort B1 >= 0.50 in >= 4/5 BPG seeds. Like-for-like control: C3 at k = 3 restricted to C4 cells.
idea.kill_criterion: Hypothesis killed ('5 metals suffice') if fixed-cohort C4 with refit B1 reaches >= 0.50 at K = 4 in >= 4/5 BPG seeds. Mixture explanation killed if, with B1 refit, kmax = 3 cells do not exceed kmax >= 4 cells by >= 0.10 R2 at the same k.
idea.expected_effect: Fixed-cohort R2: K = 4 about 0.475-0.485; K = 5 about 0.515-0.525; K = 6 about 0.55-0.57 (BISECT about +0.02 at K = 6); k* = 5, i.e. 6 measured metals, cluster lower bound near 0.48.
idea.practical_value: The honest budget statement for subset feeds and literature gap-filling: 4 metals give about 0.43-0.45 on a typical >= 10-metal series; 5 metals is a coin flip; 6 metals spaced every other one including both ends give 0.52-0.57. A '0.50 at 5 metals on C3' claim would be an artefact of small easy cells.
idea.risks: The 0.50 target is arbitrary; cohort definitions depend on the legality model; with 13 clusters the crossing interval will straddle 0.50 whatever happens (the deliverable is the curve).
idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: measurement-2; kmax-mixture decomposition, fixed-cohort C4/C5 rungs and a BISECT ladder that reframe H-BUDGET.

idea.title: Decision estimand: risk-controlled direction and separability calls with abstain-to-measure, plus net-benefit decision curves
idea.lens: decision endpoints (selective prediction with risk control; decision-curve analysis)
idea.hypothesis: With thresholds on B1's |prediction| calibrated on training folds, B1 issues direction calls on >= 50 % of strict-adjacent pairs at <= 10 % false-sign, where LINE, zero-shot G14 and a pair-type prior can issue <= 10 % at the same risk. B1's recalibrated P(|log SF| >= 0.3) gives positive net benefit over treat-all, treat-none, the prior and G14 at thresholds 0.2-0.5, also outside the dominant cluster. At full coverage B1 has no direction advantage over LINE; its value is knowing which pairs it can call.
idea.rationale: A chemist does not consume R2; they decide which pairs to trust and which candidate systems deserve a full study, at some error budget or cost ratio. Prior reports gave selective accuracy at ad hoc cut-offs without calibrated thresholds or matched-risk baselines.
idea.evidence_for: alpha = 0.10 (coverage / realised false-sign): B1 0.606 / 0.107; B0 0.508 / 0.099; LINE 0.086 / 0.118; G14 0.013 / 0.252; prior 0.032 / 0.312. alpha = 0.05: B1 0.257 / 0.068. Large clusters near nominal at alpha 0.10 (giant 0.096, phenanthroline 0.097). Net benefit at p_t 0.2 / 0.3 / 0.5: B1 0.079 / 0.061 / 0.031; G14 0.052 / 0.005 / -0.001; prior 0.046 / -0.001 / 0; non-dominant clusters B1 0.090 / 0.075 / 0.049. Brier 0.103 vs 0.130 / 0.128. Three-class separability 0.652 vs majority 0.459.
idea.evidence_against: At full coverage LINE's direction accuracy (0.744) is at least B1's (0.732) when zeros count as errors; cluster-conditional validity fails at alpha 0.10 (BTBP cluster 0.174, another 0.225) and neither Mondrian thresholds nor the window fix it; realised 0.068 at nominal 0.05; no net-benefit gain at p_t 0.1; calibration slope 0.77 (overconfident); a level-normalised conformal variant did not help.
idea.test_design: Registered E-DEC on V1 C3, k = 3, DOPT_Q; BPG decides, BP sensitivity. Conformal risk control: thresholds on |p| fitted on training folds only, alpha in {0.10, 0.05}; Mondrian by pair type as secondary. Arms at matched risk: B1 (fold beta), B0, LINE, RIDGE2, G14, pair-type sign prior. Endpoints: coverage at risk alpha and realised false-sign, pooled, per cluster, per pair type and within |y| >= 0.1; three-class separability (< 0.1, 0.1-0.3, >= 0.3) with risk-controlled abstention at 0.2 misclassification; P(SF >= 2) from cross-fold pair-type residual distributions with Platt recalibration on other folds; net benefit at p_t {0.2, 0.3, 0.5} for 'separable' and 'inseparable' decisions vs treat-all/none; calibration slope per cluster; measurements saved. Cluster bootstrap for coverage and net-benefit differences; frozen thresholds applied to any new source.
idea.kill_criterion: Killed if: pooled realised false-sign > alpha + 0.03; or B1 coverage minus the best baseline < 0.20 at alpha 0.10; or the giant or phenanthroline cluster has realised rate > 2 alpha; or delta net benefit vs the best comparator has a 90 % interval including 0 at >= 2 of 3 thresholds; or the recalibrated slope is outside [0.8, 1.25] in non-dominant clusters; or on new sources the realised rate > 0.15 at nominal 0.10. Failure in small clusters only forces a marginal-only claim.
idea.expected_effect: About 55-60 % of pairs called at about 10 % false-sign, about 25 % at 6-7 %; best non-read baseline <= 10 %; delta net benefit +0.03 to +0.06 at p_t 0.3; pooled R2 unchanged.
idea.practical_value: For a new extractant measured at 4 metals, the model says which adjacent pairs it can sign with about 90 % reliability and gives a calibrated P(SF >= 2) per pair, with the cost-ratio range in which to use it; the remaining pairs go to direct measurement.
idea.risks: Could look like endpoint switching unless registered up front; cluster-conditional failure already visible; low-|y| calls matter less (report |y| >= 0.1); never present as an R2 gain.
idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: regime-5, contrarian-4; calibrated risk control with matched-risk baselines, the full-coverage correction, net-benefit curves with explicit cost thresholds, and a cluster-conditional calibration audit.

idea.title: Pair-resolved read-policy crossing: hull-closing BISECT moves skill from the light end to the heavy end

A pair-resolved endpoint (macro mean of the 12 per-pair R2, heavy- and light-block R2) detects this with cluster intervals excluding 0; hull closure, not roughness weighting, is the lever.

idea.title: Group-cut estimand: wider pairs (dZ = 2-4, including Nd/Sm) from the same 4 reads, against a slope-only LINE and a read-free prior
idea.lens: regime / estimand reframing (cut points instead of strict neighbours)
idea.hypothesis: For dZ = 2-4 pairs (including Nd/Sm, adjacent in real feeds because Pm is absent), the same 4 DOPT_Q reads give R2 >= 0.65 with B1's form, and the skill is read-anchored interpolation, not slope: B1 beats a 2-parameter LINE through the reads by >= 0.15 and a read-free pair-type prior by >= 0.5. Registered separately; never pooled with the strict-adjacent target.
idea.rationale: Strict-adjacent pairs have the lowest signal-to-roughness ratio: per-metal roughness is fixed while signal grows with dZ. Many process decisions are about where to cut a series. The cheapest sensible alternative is LINE; if it matched B1, the claim would only be 'amplitude'.

idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: regime-4; adds the LINE and prior controls, a macro metric, a declared cut-pair set, and quantifies the substitution trap.

idea.title: Source recovery with an unbiased audit: a label-blind random sample plus the highest-stakes documents, frozen V3 rules and verified-only scoring
idea.lens: data quality and provenance (desk recovery, blind double entry)
idea.hypothesis: No-location cells hold most of B1's gain over B0. Their problem is a modest rate of gross transcription errors (decade slips, wrong figure or condition), not rounding. A blind double-entry audit of a label-free random sample estimates that rate without selection bias, and recovering the few highest-stakes documents decides whether B1's Gd term is anchored in verifiable data (B1 - B0 >= +0.02 on verified rows).
idea.rationale: Source recovery has been requested since round 3 without a protocol. Auditing only the worst-residual cells biases any V3 toward better R2 by construction; ranking by SSE share maximises information per hour but is value-informed. Combining a blind random stratum with a labelled high-stakes stratum gives both an unbiased error rate and a decisive answer on the Gd term.
idea.evidence_for: 79 C3 cells (25 publications) have no data location: 38.9 % of rows, 57.7 % of B1's SSE, 79.1 % of its gain; top 5 documents 40.5 % SSE / 44.1 % gain, top 10 49.6 % / 52.2 %; C5-BTBP alone 23.1 % / 34.6 %. ORNL-type imports are coarse (287 of 949 records have 1 significant figure). In six DOIs with both import and curated records only 9.5 % of matched values agree within 0.005 log (median |d| 0.05-0.07) and known integer-decade slips occur. Rounding variance is only 3.9 % of B1's SSE and keeping rows with >= 2 significant figures gives 0.451 vs random 0.452, so precision is not the driver. Stakes: 0.386 -> 0.422 without the import cells, which define 9 of 13 clusters.
idea.evidence_against: The no-location class mixes imports, C5-BTBP and a DMDPhPDA copy and is confounded with chemotype; recovery may simply confirm values; the most valuable documents are closed or large downloads (the user is needed); the six-DOI comparison has unmatched conditions; 15 sampled of 54 gives wide intervals (0/15 -> upper bound 0.18); auditors may still recognise numbers.
idea.test_design: (a) Software now: pre-registered condition-matching rule (DOI, metal, acid, extractant concentration, solvent, complexant; 1 % tolerance) over the 6 dual-transcribed DOIs: gross-error rate (|d log D| > 0.3 or within 0.02 of an integer decade) and sd of non-gross d adjacent log SF, with exact binomial bounds. (b) Freeze V3 rules before any recovered value is read: VERIFIED (all metals within 0.05 log for tables, 0.10 for figures with two digitisations of sd <= 0.03), MISMATCHED (source values replace), below a stated limit (censored interval targets, M23), UNLOCATABLE after a fixed search protocol, MISATTRIBUTED. (c) Two strata: a seeded label-free sample of >= 15 of the 54 import-only cells, one per publication first, frozen with a digest; and the SSE-ranked top-10 documents, labelled value-informed. (d) Two auditors transcribe blind from the source; a third adjudicates; V3 replaces only adjudicated values; references refit; V1 and V3 reported side by side; error rates extrapolated only as intervals, never as edits. (e) Score B0, B1 (fold beta) and HIST_D7 under BPG/BP on V1, V3, VERIFIED-only rows and the other cells, with a control on the 150 located cells.
idea.kill_criterion: Decisions: B1 - B0 on VERIFIED rows < +0.01 with >= 40 % of gain-carrying documents resolved -> the Gd term is reported as a prior, not a finding; >= +0.02 -> anchored, doubt closed. Import provenance stops being a quality lever if the random-sample gross-error 95 % upper bound < 5 % and sd(d adjacent log SF) < 0.03 (and part (b) is deprioritised if (a) shows 0 gross errors outside DMDPhPDA in >= 30 matched records). Fewer than 30 % of the top-10 documents locatable -> a permanent 'unverifiable' stratum reported separately.
idea.expected_effect: Most likely the C5-BTBP light-end values turn into floor-level interval targets and the DMDPhPDA copy is corrected by one decade; B1 about 0.47-0.49 on V3 with its gain shrinking to about +0.02; for imports, frequent small (about 0.05 log) disagreements and rare gross ones.
idea.practical_value: Tells users whether the Gd correction (about -0.09 log at Gd) rests on checkable measurements, whether imported database entries are trustworthy as reads, and certifies or discredits the clusters that carry all cross-chemotype evidence.
idea.risks: User time and journal access; downloads need permission; value-informed selection must stay labelled; matching rules must be frozen before looking at differences.
idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: data_quality-4, acquisition-1; a per-document SSE and gain ranking over all no-location publications, a label-blind random audit stratum that keeps V3 unbiased, frozen verified-only scoring, and the finding that precision is not the error driver.

idea.title: Label-blind SAFE + open-access novelty audit feeding a balanced, equal-weight transport check of B1
idea.lens: new data acquisition (export audit) + transport estimand reachable at small G
idea.hypothesis: SAFE records newer than the archive (+1,618, +9.6 %) plus open-access literature hold >= 10 new laboratory x chemotype units with >= 5-Ln series. That is enough for a frozen external check of whether B1's level and its sign over B0 transport to unseen laboratories (equal weight per unit), a different and reachable estimand compared with sealed delta-R2 confirmation.
idea.rationale: Confirmation of a model gain is out of reach (power <= 0.10 at G = 5-10), but a transport check of B1's level at G about 10 can tell 'transports at about 0.5' from 'collapses below 0.35'. A label-blind count of the SAFE delta is the cheapest way to learn whether such a set exists before spending the user's time.
idea.evidence_for: Equal-weight resampling of C3 units (no extra per-source noise): B1 mean 0.525 (37 publication units) and 0.50 (31 chemotype units); 95 % ranges [0.302, 0.748] / [0.364, 0.694] / [0.404, 0.642] at G = 5 / 10 / 20; P(B1 > B0) 0.80 / 0.89 / 0.95. One balanced cell per lab x chemotype gives Kish = G; Kish failure kills 26-47 % of sets at G <= 20. SAFE's schema matches the bundle.
idea.evidence_against: Equal-weight R2 is not pooled R2 and must never be quoted as 'reaching 0.50'; the resampling is optimistic (with per-source noise power is much lower); the SAFE delta may be mostly single-Ln or non-Ln records; new papers on known chemotypes add no clusters.
idea.test_design: (1) The user logs in and exports Ln records (Claude never logs in). (2) An audit script reads only metadata columns (record ID, DOI, data location, extractant name/SMILES, metal, conditions, authors) and asserts that the D column is never loaded; it computes DOIs absent from master_clean, conditions with >= 5 Ln and kmax >= 3, nearest-C3 Tanimoto (Morgan r = 2, 0.7) and family map, and laboratory identity from author sets, and outputs a pre-declared unit list plus verified open-access units. (3) If >= 10 units, freeze V-EXT: one condition per unit chosen from metadata or reads only (most metals in [-2, 2]), DOPT_Q reads, B0/B1/HIST_D7 with corpus parameters; score once; report equal-weight R2, pooled R2, per-unit B1 - B0 sign, conformal coverage and direction accuracy. (4) Record Y, detection limit and data location per unit (feeds M30 and M25).
idea.kill_criterion: Fewer than 3 new units: stop pursuing SAFE and recommend lab campaigns only. 3-9 units: descriptive check only. >= 10 units with B1's equal-weight R2 upper 95 % bound < 0.40, or B1 < B0 on > 50 % of units: B1 declared non-transportable and the deployment claim restricted to corpus-like chemistry.
idea.expected_effect: Equal-weight B1 about 0.50-0.52 with about +-0.15 at G = 10 and P(B1 > B0) about 0.9; audit yield 5-15 units (uncertain).
idea.practical_value: The only route to telling a chemist from a laboratory outside the corpus whether 4-metal predictions and their intervals hold for their kind of data, plus a go/no-go before any values are seen.
idea.risks: Unit identity must be decided from metadata before values are read; the condition rule must never use hidden metals; SAFE terms of use must be checked by the user.
idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: acquisition-4; a label-blind column contract, a unit-count go/no-go ladder and a reframing toward a transport estimand reachable at G about 10, with new resampling numbers.

idea.title: Level-stratified repeatability campaign that settles the noise ceiling and the replicate-vs-add-a-metal trade-off
idea.lens: measurement cost model + new data acquisition (H-CEILING campaign design)
idea.hypothesis: In-window laboratory repeatability of adjacent log SF has a core sd <= 0.10, and the corpus's heavy tail comes from a gross-error component concentrated at floor and ceiling levels, so the projected sigma_SF on C3's level mix stays below the 0.157-0.19 threshold. Extra read noise of sd s costs about 0.22 s^2 of pair MSE at k = 3, so duplicating reads beats adding a 5th metal only above s of about 0.14-0.15.
idea.rationale: The noise share of B1's MSE is known only to lie in [0.08, 0.87] (G1), and the ceiling threshold depends on the noise model (C10). A plain '6 systems x 3 runs at one condition' design would estimate the wrong quantity, because the out-of-window excess is a tail, not a uniformly larger sd. The same sigma decides whether labs should replicate or add metals.
idea.evidence_for: Read-noise sensitivity (Gaussian noise on the 4 reads only, D7, k = 3): R2 0.451 / 0.447 / 0.440 / 0.429 / 0.407 / 0.351 at s = 0 / 0.03 / 0.05 / 0.07 / 0.10 / 0.15; dMSE/s^2 = 0.216-0.219; a legal 5th metal is worth +0.044-0.052. Noise handles: robust per-metal 0.030-0.058, mean-square 0.107-0.188, transcription replicate 0.049, double reports 0.086; replicate noise 54 % of B1's MSE on 15 cells. The out-of-window excess is in the rms, not in the robust sd (M10).
idea.evidence_against: Six systems cannot pin a heterogeneous mean-square noise (replicated cells median 0.082 vs pooled 0.188; CV of pooled sigma^2 near 2 at n = 6); one lab measures repeatability, not reproducibility (M12); real noise is heavy-tailed (kurtosis 18.2); with ICP-MS all metals arrive together, so 'replicate vs add' becomes 'replicate vs new condition'; the five noisiest corpus replicate cells are DGA and three lie fully in window (possibly hidden-condition merges); the campaign needs lab access.
idea.test_design: (a) Software now: read-noise sensitivity curve for B1 (fold refit) under DOPT_Q and BISECT at k = 3 and 4, Gaussian and t3 noise; simulated world (dense-read D7 truths plus resampled per-metal roughness, label and read noise independent) giving the replicate-vs-add break-even sigma and the sigma_SF at which 0.50 at k = 3 becomes impossible under the actual policy (resolves C10). (b) Data-gated campaign: about 6 systems spanning DGA, branched DGA, phenanthroline diamide, a low-D-prone N-donor, malonamide, organophosphorus; two conditions each (C_in set by a one-run pilot so all 14 Ln lie in [-1.5, 1.5]; C_low with the weak end near log D -3); 3 independent runs on different days with fresh stock and organic phase plus an analytical duplicate of every phase sample; both phases assayed (mass balance within 5 %); per-metal LOD/LOQ and oxide ratios; metals <= 0.1 mM each; optionally a second operator or lab. Analysis: run-offset removal; REML variance components (analytical / run / lab); core-plus-gross-error mixture per condition; projection sigma^2 = 0.747 sigma_in^2 + 0.253 sigma_out^2; ceilings 1 - sigma^2/0.0493 and 1 - 0.67 sigma^2/0.0493. Freeze model, policy and thresholds before any value arrives.
idea.kill_criterion: (a) If the simulated break-even sigma lies outside [0.03, 0.19] under both noise shapes, the trade-off is moot (always add metals) and the analytical-repeat arm is dropped. (b) In-window core sigma_SF with lower 90 % bound >= 0.157 (or >= the simulated threshold): 0.50 at k = 3 declared noise-bound, switch to replicate-mean targets or wider pairs. Projected upper bound < 0.12 (or sigma_SF <= 0.10): the shortfall is a modelling or curation problem. Gross-error rate out >= 2x in and rms ratio >= 2: the window is adopted a priori. Otherwise extend by 3 systems.
idea.expected_effect: In-window core sigma_SF about 0.06-0.09 (ceiling 0.84-0.93); out-of-window gross-error rate several times higher; break-even about 0.14-0.15, so 'add metals' usually wins.
idea.practical_value: A stated precision for adjacent SF measured in window vs near the floor; a one-line rule on whether to repeat a determination or add a metal; the deciding experiment on whether 0.50 at k = 3 is a modelling or a measurement target; variance components for the confirmation power studies (M36).
idea.risks: Pilot uses measured levels (legitimate for design; log it); labs may report only means (insist on per-run data); third-phase or loading effects; projection assumes the corpus level mix and mechanism; simulator realism.
idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: acquisition-2, measurement-6; level-stratified two-condition design with a core-plus-gross mixture, a measured replicate-vs-add exchange rate, and a policy-specific simulated threshold, versus round 3's single-condition repeat request.

idea.title: External test of condition transfer on new non-DGA multi-condition publications
idea.lens: new data acquisition (open-access literature with provenance), confirmation of a regime
idea.hypothesis: The sibling-template gain generalises beyond DGA: on new non-DGA multi-condition publications the median per-publication relative pair-SSE reduction of the frozen template vs B1 is > 0 on in-window rows.
idea.rationale: Stratified in-corpus checks suggest the gain is a DGA phenomenon plus out-of-window rows. Only new non-DGA multi-condition series, read after freezing, can settle this, and several verified open-access candidates are exactly such designs (acid, extractant concentration and diluent scans).
idea.evidence_for: E6 reproduced (0.573 vs 0.449); 14/19 publications positive; roughness r +0.36 within publication x extractant. Verified open-access multi-condition non-DGA candidates exist (phenanthroline-diamide diluent and acid scans with numeric SI tables, a phosphonium nitrate system, organophosphorus acid in two diluents). Figure-sourced cells are not rougher than table cells, so plotted-only sources are admissible (M22).
idea.evidence_against: In C3: sc009 0.700 vs 0.515; non-sc009 0.485 vs 0.400; non-sc009 in-window rows 0.569 vs B1 0.598 (no gain); only 4/7 non-sc009 publications positive and three N-donor/amide publications lose (-0.26 to -0.37). Power: 0.40-0.45 at 5 publications, 0.50-0.53 at 6, 0.76 at 10, 0.84 at 12 (weaker under the non-DGA distribution). Diluent changes are larger perturbations than acid changes. Automated search yield is low.
idea.test_design: Register E-SIB before extraction: anchor = condition with most in-window metals; template rule frozen from M01/M03; near-copy exclusion; DOPT_Q at 4 reads with 2- and 3-read ladder. An analyst extracts each series (two independent digitisations for plots) and gives the scorer only the anchor series and the read metals of each target condition. Score all strict-adjacent pairs with SIB, B1 (frozen corpus beta) and copy-sibling. Primary: per-publication relative pair-SSE of SIB vs B1, in-window and all rows separately. Controls: B1, copy-sibling, other-extractant shuffled sibling. Add the user's own lab series where available. Check authors and ligands for overlap with corpus groups first; skip any figure without D on the axis.
idea.kill_criterion: With >= 6 new non-DGA publications: median gain <= 0 on in-window rows, or <= 3/6 positive, declares the sibling gain DGA- or shared-artefact-specific and B1 is recommended for non-DGA users. >= 5/6 positive with median >= 0.15 promotes the regime, pending >= 10 publications.
idea.expected_effect: Prior: about 0 for in-window non-DGA rows; likely mixed signs across publications.
idea.practical_value: Answers a process chemist's question: with one full series of this ligand, after changing acid or diluent, can 4 metals be trusted for adjacent SFs, and for which donor classes.
idea.risks: Candidate list chosen after the stratification (lead); digitisation and unit conversions; author overlap; one publication carries many rows (analyse at publication level); no downloads without the user's permission.
idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: acquisition-3; the in-window non-DGA null (0.569 vs 0.598) and per-publication power numbers are new, as is targeting open-access multi-condition non-DGA designs.

idea.title: Inter-laboratory reproducibility of adjacent log SF: matched-condition literature meta-analysis first, ring test second
idea.lens: meta-analysis of laboratory effects + balanced reproducibility campaign
idea.hypothesis: The programme's cross-publication failure is either a laboratory signature (labs measure different adjacent SF for the same system and condition; roughness reproduces within lab, not between) or condition mismatch (labs agree at matched conditions, between-lab tau^2 <= 0.005). Two staged measurements decide between them.
idea.rationale: Every cross-source null of rounds 1-4 has these two readings. H-CEILING targets within-lab repeatability only; between-lab reproducibility has never been estimated, yet it bounds every BP/BPG model, decides whether the publication is a valid confirmation unit, and decides whether the sibling gain transfers to a user's own lab.
idea.evidence_for: Matched-condition, different-publication pairs: MSE 0.021 (5 pairs) vs unmatched 0.048 (835) vs same-publication matched 0.030. Within a lab, copy error rises with |dlog acid| (rho +0.30). Roughness r +0.36 / +0.14 / -0.02; cross-publication copy R2 -0.08; hidden heavy-metal mean level errors all positive (consistent with, not proof of, an analytical bias); the archive records no analytical method.
idea.evidence_against: Five matched pairs are an anecdote; level-nearest cross-publication templates still fail (0.164 vs 0.499); the oxide-interference model was no better than placebo (M06); a ring test is costly and labs may harmonise informally; matched replicates may be too rare to find.
idea.test_design: Stage 1 (software plus literature; needs the user's access, no downloads without permission): count matched cross-publication pairs per system in master_clean and V1 under pre-declared tolerances (same acid type, |dlog acid| <= 0.1, |dlog L| <= 0.1, same diluent class); harvest independent measurements of the systems with most labs (tables and SI first; figures only through M22's verified digitisation); random-effects model per pair type with condition strata; report tau^2, I^2 and the implied cross-source cap; analysis plan frozen before any harvested value is read. Stage 2 (if Stage 1 has < 30 comparisons from >= 6 labs or is inconclusive): 2 systems (a TODGA reference and a phenanthroline diamide) x 4 labs x 3 runs at one SOP placing all Ln in log D [-1.5, 1.5]; shared extractant batch and feed plus one own-feed run; raw intensities, isotopes, interference corrections and LOD reported; variance components; within- vs between-lab roughness correlation (12 lab-pair x system comparisons); reprocessing with and without interference correction.
idea.kill_criterion: Lab signature supported (close cross-source modelling together with M08; lab becomes the confirmation unit; sibling regime same-lab only) if tau^2 >= 0.02 with lower bound > 0.01, or between-lab roughness r < 0.15 with within-lab r >= 0.30. Lab-bias explanation killed (condition-matched cross-lab regime and condition-aware cross-publication models reopened; publication unit downgraded) if tau^2 <= 0.005, or between-lab r >= 0.30 with sigma_between <= 1.2 sigma_within. Stage 1 is uninformative if < 30 matched comparisons from >= 6 labs exist.
idea.expected_effect: The first number for inter-laboratory reproducibility of adjacent log SF and an explicit upper bound on any BP/BPG model; prior leans toward a laboratory signature.
idea.practical_value: How far to trust a literature adjacent SF from another lab for the user's system; an inter-lab uncertainty to carry into stage-count calculations (for SF 1.2-1.5 a 0.1-log spread changes stage counts materially); whether interference corrections must be reported with published SFs.
idea.risks: Scarce matched replicates; publication bias toward agreement; incomplete condition metadata; recruiting labs is slow; results for two systems may not generalise.
idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: acquisition-5, contrarian-6; reproducibility (not repeatability) across labs, staged from a cheap desk meta-analysis to a ring test with an analytical-interference control.

idea.title: Aqueous-complexant rule: an aqueous complexing agent cancels or inverts the Gd term
idea.lens: physics and chemistry (log D as organic minus aqueous speciation)
idea.hypothesis: The Gd dip in log D is the Gd anomaly of the extracted complex minus that of the aqueous species. In nitrate-only media the aqueous species is the aqua/nitrato ion and a negative dip appears (B1's beta about -0.09). When an aqueous complexing agent (aminopolycarboxylate or N-donor) dominates aqueous speciation, its own Gd anomaly is subtracted and cancels or inverts the dip. So B1's Gd term is wrong in sign in these cells, and a label-free rule (Gd term off when an aqueous complexant is present; inert nitrate salts do not count) removes a systematic error.
idea.rationale: The form is exact from mass balance (log D = log D0 - log(1 + sum beta_aq [L]^n)). It was stated as a data-contract rule but never scored. The decisive feature is a within-laboratory negative control: the same publications contain complexant cells and nitrate-salt-only cells with the same extractant and acid range.
idea.evidence_for: Bench Gd chord: complexant + NaNO3 cells +0.088 (6 cells, none negative); NaNO3-only cells of the same publications -0.092; no complexant -0.126 (118 cells). Projected residuals show a Gd bump for complexants and a dip for NaNO3. In complexant cells B1 is worse than B0 (SSE 1.73 vs 1.35 per seed); E3 also reports negative Gd gain there. Rule 'Gd term off in the 15 complexant cells': BPG 0.4521 -> 0.4575; complexant rows 0.398 -> 0.469; placebo (15 random non-complexant cells, 300 draws) mean 0.4494, 95 % [0.4463, 0.4521], max 0.4536. Tabulated stability constants put the aminopolycarboxylate's own Gd chord near -0.09.
idea.evidence_against: Only 15 cells from 3 publications, all sc009 in the giant cluster (Kish about 1); the rule was checked after E3 had seen negative gain (lead); the observed shift (+0.18) is about twice the tabulated prediction and a magnitude variant scored below plain switch-off; some mixed-complexant cells give dip-like signs; complexant identity is not on the bench (it comes from provenance).
idea.test_design: (a) Freeze an aqueous-complexant list before scoring (from provenance; inert nitrate salts excluded). (b) B1-AQ = B1 with the Gd potential set to 0 in complexant cells, beta fitted per fold on non-complexant training cells; secondary B1-AQb with u_Gd = beta - c_Gd(complexant) from tabulated constants where available. (c) Score BPG (deciding) and BP pooled R2, the complexant stratum (about 131 rows per seed), Eu/Gd and Gd/Tb R2, balanced MAE. (d) Controls: placebo distribution (Gd off in 15 random non-complexant cells, 1,000 draws); NaNO3-only negative control whose chord must stay < 0 and to which the rule does not apply; per-publication sign of the complexant chord. (e) Decisive external check: paired series from the same laboratory with and without an aqueous complexant, read before any model change; prediction: the Gd chord rises with the complexant in each pair.
idea.kill_criterion: Killed if B1-AQ does not exceed the 97.5th percentile of the placebo in >= 4/5 BPG seeds; or dropping any one of the 3 publications removes > 70 % of the gain; or, externally, in >= 2 of 3 paired series from >= 2 laboratories the Gd chord does not rise when the complexant is added.
idea.expected_effect: +0.004 to +0.006 pooled R2 (an in-corpus lead below the margin); complexant-stratum R2 about 0.40 -> 0.47; large for Gd pairs of any future complexant-containing source; externally a sign prediction (dip -> null or bump).
idea.practical_value: Separation schemes that add an aqueous complexing agent are where Gd/Eu and Tb/Gd cuts are often tuned; the rule warns that such agents erase the Gd anomaly, so B1 would mispredict whether Gd follows Eu or Tb. Data contract: record complexant identity and free concentration; never apply the universal Gd term blindly.
idea.risks: One laboratory family cannot separate 'complexant' from 'this lab's protocol' (the same-lab NaNO3 control mitigates but does not eliminate this); post hoc; tabulated constants depend on medium and ionic strength (keep the magnitude variant secondary).
idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: physics-1; first scored version of the aqueous-speciation subtraction, with a same-laboratory negative control, a placebo-calibrated score and an external paired-series falsification design.
