idea.title: Pre-slot decidability gate (class ceiling, development MDE, P(level >= target) band, training-size check), replayed on rounds 3-4
idea.lens: evaluation design (prospective power and decidability)
idea.hypothesis: Four checks that do not look at a slot's outcome (cross-fitted ceiling of the hypothesis class >= the margin; development MDE <= the plausible effect; for level claims, cluster probability P(level >= 0.50) outside [0.2, 0.8]; for learned models, ability to beat B1 with about 60 training cells in the non-giant folds) would have retired all five round-4 losers and a pass/fail 'k = 4 reaches 0.50' slot, while passing B1 - B0.
idea.rationale: Round 4 spent 5 slots on contrasts of -0.024 to -0.0001 whose class ceilings were below the margin even as oracles; one fold decides and trains on 51-69 cells; the 0.50 aspiration sits inside a cluster interval of about +-0.05, so 'reaches 0.50' is a coin flip at current estimates.
idea.evidence_for: Ceilings: donor x pair-type cross-fit -0.041 and oracle +0.0004 balanced MAE, so S01 and S02 retire. MDE: S05 - B1 0.011 and S11 - B1 0.003 vs plausible effects <= 0.005 / <= 0.002 (diagnostics only); B1 - B0 passes (equal-weight IM t 2.6). Level band (2,000 cluster draws): B1 all rows 0.452 [0.394, 0.508], P(>= 0.50) 0.03; B1 inside the window 0.540 [0.448, 0.576], P 0.80; the k = 4 estimate 0.495-0.503 sits at P about 0.5 by construction. The giant cluster holds 162 of 229 cells, so cluster-isolating designs train it on <= 67 cells.
idea.evidence_against: A noisy ceiling estimate can kill a true effect; the MDE needs a pilot estimate of how far the candidate departs from B1; the bootstrap under-covers at Kish 2.24 so P(>= 0.50) is approximate; a learned model may need > 60 cells and still be useful in other regimes.
idea.test_design: Before each slot compute: (a) the cross-fitted ceiling of the hypothesis class under BPG (leave-own-chemotype or leave-own-cluster shift of B1's residual on the class's features); (b) the development MDE at 80 % for the registered test (M34/M35) from a one-seed pilot's per-cluster dSSE spread; (c) for level claims, the cluster-bootstrap P(level >= target); (d) for learned models, non-giant-fold dSSE when trained on 5 random 60-cell subsets vs the full ~209 cells. Run as a decision slot only if ceiling >= 2 % SSE, MDE <= plausible effect, P outside [0.2, 0.8], and no > 60-cell requirement; otherwise run as a labelled diagnostic. Level claims failing the band report the paired increment (k = 4 minus k = 3, about +0.044-0.052) and the k at which P >= 0.8. Freeze thresholds, then replay on S01, S02, S05, S06, S11, B2, R02, R14/B1 and the Gd term.
idea.kill_criterion: Gate dropped as miscalibrated if the replay retires B1 - B0 or the Gd term, or lets >= 2 of the 5 round-4 losers through as decision slots. Check (d) alone dropped if 60-cell and full training show no difference for S02 and S05.
idea.expected_effect: Fewer, better-powered decision slots in round 5; the 0.50 aspiration reported as P(level >= 0.50) with an interval rather than a pass/fail point.
idea.practical_value: Stops spending compute and analyst degrees of freedom on questions the corpus cannot answer; statements such as 'five measured metals reach 0.50' come with the probability that they hold for new sources.
idea.risks: Tuning the gate's thresholds after the replay adds another forking path; freeze them first.
idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: evaluation-7; one pre-slot gate combining class ceiling, MDE, a level band and a training-size check, with a replay it must pass on B1 - B0.

idea.title: In-window non-DGA Gd-triad acquisition sized from the measured between-unit spread of the Gd dip
idea.lens: new data acquisition (non-DGA Gd-triad series) for the donor dependence of B1's only transferable effect
idea.hypothesis: In new non-DGA laboratory x extractant units measured with Eu, Gd and Tb all inside log D [-2, 2], the mean Gd dip is <= -0.12 log, against about -0.04 for in-window DGA units and B1's universal beta of -0.094. The donor dependence of the Gd effect is then chemistry that carries over to new laboratories.
idea.rationale: B1's gain (94 % from Eu/Gd and Gd/Tb) is learned mostly from two provenance-pending non-DGA sources, Gd-query Kish is 2.33, and every held-out donor-class test was null on about 5 non-DGA clusters. Exploratory checks show the dip is window-inflated, so new data must be in window or donor differences stay confounded with floor artefacts, and the measured between-unit spread fixes the sample size.
idea.evidence_for: Dip out vs in window: DGA -0.109 vs -0.034; non-DGA -0.287 vs -0.146. In-window unit level: non-DGA -0.144 (29 extractant x publication units, sd 0.138) vs DGA -0.040 (26 units). Family chords DGA -0.053, amide -0.184, N-heterocyclic -0.209; phenanthroline diamides with V-shaped D-vs-Z curves minimal at Gd have been reported. Only Sm-Dy plus anchors are needed, which many papers report.
idea.evidence_against: A family Gd scale is +0.014 in sample but -0.001 to -0.004 under LOCO, and a per-chemotype amplitude gives no gain; power vs -0.072 if the true mean is -0.144: 0.30 / 0.45 / 0.64 / about 0.73 at 6 / 10 / 16 / 20 units (95 % half-widths 0.145 / 0.099 / 0.074 at 6 / 10 / 16); within a unit the condition-to-condition sd of the dip is 0.088, so each unit needs >= 2 conditions; open-access N-donor papers cluster in a few groups.
idea.test_design: Acquire >= 16 (target 20) new non-DGA units, each a distinct laboratory x extractant, from open access, the SAFE audit (M33) and lab series (M11). Inclusion frozen: Sm, Eu, Gd, Tb, Dy measured; Eu, Gd, Tb within [-2, 2]; >= 2 conditions averaged; detection limit stated or derivable. Statistic: dip = log D(Gd) minus the Eu-Tb chord along -r(CN8), averaged per unit. Tests: one-sample vs -0.072; Welch vs the 26 in-window C3 DGA units. Prospective check on new units at k = 3 (reads exclude Gd): B1 with universal beta vs B1 with a non-DGA beta frozen now from the C3 in-window non-DGA units through B1's own projection; paired per-unit sign as decision statistic. Count units by laboratory and stratify by group; report how many candidates the in-window rule excluded.
idea.kill_criterion: With >= 16 units: killed if the new non-DGA mean dip has a 95 % CI including -0.072, or the frozen non-DGA beta beats the universal beta on <= 50 % of units (donor dependence is then a property of the corpus's few non-DGA sources and the universal Gd term stays). Confirmed if the CI lies below -0.10 and the class beta wins on >= 70 % of units.
idea.expected_effect: If chemistry: mean about -0.14 and a 10-20 % reduction of Eu/Gd + Gd/Tb SSE on N-donor units (descriptive, not a pooled R2 claim). If floor or provenance: about -0.07 to -0.09.
idea.practical_value: Gives a chemist screening N-donor or amide ligands for Eu/Gd and Gd/Tb cuts a defensible Gd correction ('for N-donors expect Gd about 0.14 log below the Eu-Tb chord') and says whether it is safe to rely on before measuring Gd.
idea.risks: Hidden lab effects in clustered author groups; the dip-to-beta conversion must not be refitted; the in-window rule may exclude the most selective ligands.
idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: acquisition-6; the measured window inflation of the dip, the in-window unit-level contrast, the between-unit sd and resulting sample sizes, and a prospective frozen-beta check.

idea.title: Value-of-prior-information ladder (S0-S4), with the same-publication other-extractant channel split into homologue chemistry vs laboratory fingerprint
idea.lens: regime / estimand reframing (knowledge states) + meta-analysis of laboratory effects with placebo channels
idea.hypothesis: Information beyond B1 is laboratory-local and extractant-specific: other labs' curves of the same chemotype (S1) or extractant (S2) add < +0.02 without C5-BTBP; the lab's own data on other extractants (S3) add +0.01 to +0.05, and that part comes from same-chemotype homologues rather than a generic laboratory or analytical fingerprint; only the lab's own series of the same extractant (S4) add >= +0.10. S0 (nothing known) stays the primary estimand.
idea.rationale: A chemist planning a 4-metal campaign must decide what prior information to collect. Round 4 posed only S0. If S3 were an instrument fingerprint, a lab could calibrate it once (a cheap product); if it is homologue chemistry, the deployable regime is a ligand-design lab's own homologue history. The two explanations of the same channel compete and are tested together.
idea.evidence_for: S1: blend +0.015 without C5-BTBP. S2: +0.008 without C5-BTBP (the 50/50 blend looks like +0.051 with it). S3: publication x pair offsets K = 5 / 10 give 0.474 / 0.478 vs B1 0.455 (K = 0: 0.291); on cells without a same-extractant sibling 0.460 vs 0.412. Channel split: other extractant same publication 0.4624 vs other chemotype same publication 0.4534 vs B1 0.4521; random-publication placebo 0.414-0.441; homologue rows 0.4888 vs 0.4666. S4: 0.580-0.594. Roughness r +0.36 / +0.14 / -0.02. An oxide-interference model predicts roughness at r -0.05, no better than shifted-table placebos; the Gd dip is larger at small Pr:Gd ratio, opposite to the artefact prediction.

idea.test_design: Define S0-S4 from metadata only; score each on its own eligible C3 rows at k = 3 DOPT_Q vs B1 on the same rows. Frozen predictor family: template blend with weight chosen leave-one-cluster-out; group x pair offsets K in {5, 10} (20 as sensitivity); for S3, separate homologue (same chemotype) and other-chemotype channels, and lab x metal level offsets vs pair offsets (calibration test); a homologue template. Hold-out for S3: one extractant (all its conditions) within publications with >= 2 extractants. Controls: random-publication placebo, copy-group exclusion, without C5-BTBP, inside the window. Inference unit publication (S3, S4) or cluster (S1, S2). Contrasts S2-S1, homologue - other chemotype, level vs pair offsets, S4-S3. Output a 5-row value-of-information table, each row its own estimand. One pre-declared refit of the interference model where isotopes are recorded.
idea.kill_criterion: Lab-local thesis killed if S1 or S2 reaches >= +0.03 without C5-BTBP with leave-one-cluster-out weights and a positive bootstrap lower bound. S3 killed if < +0.01 at both K or < 60 % of publications improve. Homologue claim killed if homologue - B1 < +0.01 (or lower bound <= 0), if its sign flips when either contributing cluster is left out, or if other-chemotype >= homologue. Calibration explanation dropped if level offsets do not match or beat pair offsets.
idea.expected_effect: S1 +0.01 to +0.02; S2 about +0.01; S3 +0.01 to +0.04, mostly homologue; S4 +0.10 to +0.17; S0 unchanged at 0.452.

idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: regime-2, contrarian-5; splits the within-source regime into knowledge states with specificity contrasts, answers G2's other-extractant share, and falsifies the analytical-fingerprint explanation.

idea.title: Ce: reliability first, a registered null for Ce modelling, and a discriminating experiment (redox state vs contamination vs chemistry)
idea.lens: data quality (test-retest reliability) + physics and chemistry of the Ce anomaly
idea.hypothesis: Ce's deviation from the La-Pr chord (La/Ce + Ce/Pr = 34.2 % of B1's SSE) is a one-signed, sporadic per-sample excess (partial Ce(IV) under oxidising nitrate conditions, blank or contamination, or an analytical spike) with near-zero test-retest reliability. No universal, conditional or transferred Ce term helps under source hold-out; only measuring Ce reduces this error.
idea.rationale: The project's reliability-before-correlation rule requires a replicate check of a derived quantity before correlating it with conditions. If the Ce deviation does not reproduce between series of the same cell, H-CE's condition gate has no power and a null would be uninformative. Physics gives sharp discriminating predictions (Ce(IV) needs nitrate and oxidising conditions; contamination scales with 1/concentration; a chemical tetrad would lift Ce and Pr together).
idea.evidence_for: Split-series ICC (cells with >= 2 source series): Ce -0.06 (6 cells, 12 series) vs Nd 0.84, Eu 0.77, Pr 0.30. ICC by extractant 0.09, by publication 0.03. Ce chord right-skewed (skew +1.65; p05 / p50 / p95 -0.19 / +0.03 / +0.43) vs Pr -1.22; convex-tetrad prediction fails (Ce +0.056 vs Pr +0.001). Within publication, Ce vs acid -0.34 -> -0.11 (p 0.24) and Ce vs level -0.31 -> -0.02; Ce vs HCl within publication +0.19, against a Ce(IV) reading. A universal Ce potential gives +0.004 in sample but 0.000 under leave-cluster-out and leave-chemotype-out, all from C5-BTBP; cross-publication Ce transfer hurts (0.421 vs 0.427); asymmetric Ce intervals no better. In one cell figure and table differ by -0.71 at Ce.
idea.evidence_against: Tiny n (6 cells); some 'series' are hidden-condition merges, which bias ICC down; Ce reproduces somewhat within extractant x publication; the corpus has no redox or blank metadata; M28 reports a within-publication Spearman of -0.23 and a leave-cluster-out gain of +0.009 for a Ce acid term on hidden-level errors, a direct conflict that this idea and M28 must resolve together.
idea.test_design: 1. Enlarge the replicate set without new data: bench cells with nrep >= 2, archive value-conflict groups under identical condition keys with full La-Ce-Pr triplets, round 3's 15 replicated cells; exclude merge cells. Per-metal split-series ICC(1) with cell-cluster bootstrap; signal-injection check (add a 0.15 per-cell Ce offset) to show the design can detect reproducibility. 2. Registered diagnostic null: B1 + Ce with gamma fitted per fold, BPG and BP; within-publication analysis of Ce vs acid, extractant concentration, HCl vs HNO3, level and contact time with publication-demeaned ranks and publication bootstrap; La/Ce + Ce/Pr subgroup reported in every round-5 table. 3. Data-gated paired experiments in one DGA/HNO3 system with trace Ce: HNO3 vs HCl at matched D; fresh vs aged Ce(III) stock and with vs without a mild reductant; two metal concentrations 10x apart plus process blanks. Predictions: Ce(IV) -> excess vanishes in HCl or with reductant and is independent of concentration; contamination -> excess scales as 1/concentration and appears in blanks; chemistry -> identical in all arms.
idea.kill_criterion: Ce modelling closed (routed to measurement and widened intervals) if the upper ICC_Ce bound < 0.3. Null falsified and Ce modelling reopened (M28) if ICC_Ce has a lower bound > 0.3 on >= 15 replicate cells, or fold-fitted B1 + Ce gives >= +0.005 in >= 4/5 BPG seeds with positive SSE change in >= 3 clusters besides C5-BTBP's, or a within-publication condition correlation has |rho| >= 0.3 with a CI excluding 0. If injected-signal recovery fails, the result is 'not decidable'. Mechanisms are decided by the experimental arms.
idea.expected_effect: No R2 change by design; saves round-5 slots on the largest error block; a likely closure of H-CE plus a mechanism answer from the experiment.
idea.practical_value: If a process depends on La/Ce or Ce/Pr, measure Ce, because no model trained on other sources predicts it; widen Ce-pair intervals. If the excess is Ce(IV), redox control of the feed is itself a separation lever and must be reported; curators should record Ce oxidation state, reductants and blanks.
idea.risks: A registered null can be misread as 'no Ce chemistry' (wording: not transferable at this corpus size); replicate set may stay below 15 cells; merged-condition contamination; the experiment needs a lab.
idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: data_quality-6, physics-5; puts a replicate reliability check and a registered null before H-CE's condition gate, runs the within-publication analysis (gap G5), and adds a physically discriminating experiment.

idea.title: Nested re-estimation of the five post hoc leads before registration (window, K, edge damping, half-slope, max-min 5th read)
idea.lens: evaluation design (selection optimism)
idea.hypothesis: Re-running each analyst's selection step inside the outer folds (choose on the other folds' OOF rows, apply to the held-out fold) exposes a measurable optimism for each lead. Leads that still meet their decision thresholds after nesting can be registered; the rest are retired or kept as diagnostics.
idea.rationale: The evidence base lists five post hoc choices as leads, not results, and round 4 showed inner selection was optimistic (outer SSE worse in 12 of 14 fold-fits that chose a correction). A nested replay prices the selection step on the same data without new data.
idea.evidence_for: Window: nested half-width choice (inside R2 at coverage >= 0.70) gives 0.527 at 75.3 % vs 0.540 post hoc; h = 2 chosen in 21 of 25 folds; the curve is monotone (h 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.0 / 2.5 / 3.0: coverage 45.5 / 60 / 75 / 85 / 93 %, inside R2 0.571 / 0.557 / 0.540 / 0.501 / 0.495), so [-2, 2] is not a peak. Matched-coverage controls: random abstention stratified by pair type x cluster 0.477 [0.466, 0.488] (max 0.493); dropping La/Ce, Ce/Pr, Pr/Nd 0.466 at 78 %; dropping out-of-hull rows 0.472 at 88 %. Publication x pair offsets: best fixed K = 5 (0.533); nested choice 0.526 (K = 5 in 16 of 25 folds).
idea.evidence_against: Nesting on the same 229 cells removes selection optimism within the grid but not the choice of grid, estimator family or idea; the window abstains on 81 % of the BTBP cluster's rows, so part of its gain is provenance; levels near 0.53 carry a cluster interval of about +-0.05 (M38).
idea.test_design: 1. Freeze the grids the analysts actually considered: window (the 4 published windows plus a 6-point half-width grid); K in {0, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50}; edge damping d in {0, 0.25, 0.375, 0.5, 0.75, 1} (covers the half-slope rule); 5th-read policy in {random, max-min, DOPT_Q-nested, Gd-first, BISECT}. 2. Fix the selection criterion in advance (SSE, or inside R2 at coverage >= 0.70). 3. Per seed and outer fold select on the other folds' OOF rows and apply to the held-out fold; pool folds, average seeds. 4. Report nested value, optimism (post hoc minus nested), share of folds choosing the post hoc value, cluster intervals. 5. Controls: stratified random abstention and drop-light-pairs (window); noise-matched linear tail (edge); random legal read on identical queries (5th read). 6. Register the window as the full coverage-R2 curve with operating points at coverage 0.75 and 0.90 fixed now (shared with M09).
idea.kill_criterion: A lead is retired if its nested value misses its threshold (window: inside R2 < 0.50 at coverage >= 0.70, or not above the stratified control by >= 0.03; publication offsets: < B1 + 0.02; edge continuation: < +0.003; max-min 5th read: < DOPT_Q-nested + 0.005), or if its post hoc value is chosen in fewer than 50 % of folds.
idea.expected_effect: Window survives (about 0.527 at 75 %, about +0.05 over the stratified control); publication offsets survive (0.526); edge rules and max-min shrink to about +0.002-0.004 and +-0.005 and are retired or kept as diagnostics.
idea.practical_value: Honest numbers before they are advertised ('when both predicted log D lie in [-2, 2], expect R2 about 0.53 on three quarters of pairs; outside about 0.30'), and fewer round-5 slots spent on leads that only look good after selection.
idea.risks: A nested value is a debiased lead, not a result; the window's operating points must be fixed now and labelled as fixed after this analysis.
idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: evaluation-3; nested values for two of the five leads, the monotone curve showing [-2, 2] is not a peak, and stratified and cheapest-alternative controls.

idea.title: Low-read operating point inside condition transfer: 2 reads plus a sibling vs B1 at 4 reads, with an additive shift-plus-tilt deformation model and a proportional-scaling control
idea.lens: measurement design (k ladder, cost model) + physics of condition change (slope analysis)
idea.hypothesis: For the same extractant in the same laboratory, a condition change mainly shifts every Ln equally and adds a smooth tilt, while metal-specific anomalies stay fixed. So 2 well-placed reads at the new condition plus a sibling template predict adjacent log SF at least as well as B1 with 4 reads and no sibling, and additive deformation beats proportional (LFER) rescaling of the template.
idea.rationale: In the condition-transfer regime the expensive unit is the condition, and gap G2 lists k = 0-2 behaviour as unreported. Slope analysis gives a pre-declarable family of deformations ordered by the reads they need (copy, shift, shift+tilt, full PWL), which turns the low-read ladder into a falsifiable physical claim rather than a tuning exercise.
idea.evidence_for:
Exploratory, E6 rows, DOPT_Q reads.
- SIB with 2 DOPT_Q-nested reads 0.517 vs D7 with 4 reads 0.447; near-copies excluded 0.490 vs 0.423.
- Near-copies excluded: dominant cluster 0.602 vs 0.500 (75 cells); other clusters 0.408 vs 0.366 (27 cells).
- Shift only (1 read) = copy 0.411: a pure shift cancels in log SF, as predicted.
- 2 extreme reads 0.492; 2 middle reads 0.441 (tilt needs a lever arm).
- Additive 4-read template 0.573 vs LFER-scaled 0.525.
- Gd chord does not move with acid within an extractant (rho 0.07, n 61).
idea.evidence_against:
- 2-read placement is unsettled: extremes-first is worse than DOPT_Q-nested 2 reads (0.489-0.492 vs 0.517), and the 2-read subsets were taken from DOPT_Q 4-read sets, not designed.
- Going from 2 to 4 reads adds about +0.08, so the change is more than shift + tilt.
- At shape sd >= 0.05 the 2-read advantage vanishes (+0.009); only 27 cells lie outside the dominant cluster.
- Single-sibling templates are poor (M01); template rules were chosen on these cells.
idea.test_design: Inside E-CT (M01), condition hold-out within publication x extractant, pre-declared near-copy exclusion (shape sd < 0.02). Deformation ladder on identical rows: D0 copy; D1 shift (1 read, lightest measured metal); D2 shift+tilt with the lightest and heaviest measured metals (label-free); D2-DOPT (DOPT_Q-nested 2 reads); D2-LS (least-squares shift+tilt on the 4 reads, no PWL); D4 additive PWL; negative control D4-scaled (proportional LFER). Baselines B1 at 4 reads and B1 at 2 reads (same metals). Primary contrast SIB at 2 reads - B1 at 4 reads, cluster_cpg intervals, split dominant cluster vs rest and by condition-distance tertile; balanced MAE.
idea.kill_criterion: Killed if: SIB(2 reads) - B1(4 reads) <= 0 in the near-copy-excluded, non-dominant-cluster stratum; or the overall cluster lower bound < -0.02; or D2 fails to beat B1(4 reads) by >= +0.02 in >= 4/5 seeds after near-copy exclusion; or the gain disappears when the template is the single nearest condition instead of the mean; or D4-scaled >= D4 (refutes the additive model).
idea.expected_effect: SIB(2 reads) - B1(4 reads) about +0.04 to +0.10; D2 about 0.47-0.49 vs B1 about 0.43-0.45 after near-copy exclusion; D4 near 0.55-0.57.
idea.practical_value: After one or more full series of an extractant, each new acidity, concentration or diluent needs only 2 metals (which 2 is decided by the test) to match a 4-metal measurement without a reference. Shift and tilt the old series; do not rescale it. Halves the assay load wherever each metal costs a separate determination, and lets literature miners complete partial series within a paper.
idea.risks: Near-copies and shared stocks inflate every sibling number; curves that turn over at the heavy end may break shift+tilt; separate estimand only; post hoc template rules.
idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: measurement-3, physics-3; fills the k < 3 part of G2, refutes proportional deformation (0.525 vs 0.573), and records the open conflict on 2-read placement (extremes 0.489-0.492 vs DOPT_Q-nested 0.517) as a pre-declared crossing.

idea.title: Choose conditions, not metals: active selection of which conditions get full series
idea.lens: active learning over the real cost unit (the experiment)
idea.hypothesis: A lab characterising one extractant across C conditions first screens every condition with 4 reads, then measures full series at conditions spread over the screen-level quantiles (SPREAD) and predicts the rest from them. This predicts the remaining conditions better than random, central or extreme choices and reaches R2 >= 0.50 with 2 full series.
idea.rationale: With ICP-MS the cost unit is the experiment, and metal-placement policies are exhausted at k = 3 (+0.006). Nobody has optimised which conditions to characterise fully. Template quality depends on level matching (M03), so library coverage of the level range is the natural objective.
idea.evidence_for: 11 families with >= 5 C3 cells, non-library rows. n = 2: SPREAD 0.541, CENTRAL 0.497, RANDOM 0.401, EXTREME -0.03, B1 0.425. n = 3: 0.557 / 0.440 / 0.462 / 0.075 / 0.40. idea.test_design: Registered simulation on all C3 families with >= 4 cells, BPG DOPT_Q reads, 5 seeds, budgets n = 1-3 full series. idea.title: Variance budget of B1's residual (transferable / laboratory-shared / target-specific) with a sibling dose-response ceiling and a registered futility rule for 0.50 under BPG
idea.lens: crossed random effects, noise-ceiling bounds, stop rule
idea.hypothesis: B1's residual splits into a transferable part (chemotype or extractant x pair, declared condition slopes), a laboratory-shared part (publication, extractant x publication, condition kernel) and a target-specific part. The transferable part is below the 8.8 % of SSE needed to reach 0.50, and the target-specific part is >= 50 % of B1's MSE, so 0.50 at k = 3 under BPG is out of reach for cross-source models in the declared feature classes.
idea.rationale: Routes have been closed one by one with weak power caveats. A joint budget answers once how much residual is reachable in principle for a new laboratory, how much needs a lab reference series, and how much is noise or idiosyncratic. A sibling-count dose-response gives an independent, model-free estimate of the unreachable part without a lab campaign.
idea.evidence_for: Sibling dose-response (103 cells with >= 4 siblings): MSE(n) = a + b/n with a 0.0174, b 0.0179; a/B1 MSE 0.67 (0.59 without C5-BTBP); cap 0.584 vs B1 0.378 on those rows. Relation-class residual correlations: other extractant same publication 0.16 (similar for same and different chemotype, i.e. lab-like); same extractant same publication 0.36 (0.51 at near-identical conditions); same extractant other publication 0.10-0.14. Chemotype x pair offsets from other publications <= +0.006; cross-publication and analog templates do not beat B1 (0.404 vs 0.499; blend 0.4512 vs 0.4521). Near-condition bound: non-shared share of pair error <= 0.49 (mean-square) / 0.24 (rank). a/B1 close to the 15-cell replicate share 0.54.
idea.evidence_against: Family-rich cells are about 45 % of rows and DGA-heavy; a includes condition-specific chemistry a condition-aware model might reach (copy error rises with |dlog acid|, rho +0.30); the 1/n fit has 4 points and heavy tails (dropping C5-BTBP halves a); with about 4 effective chemotypes the transferable interval may be too wide; futility is conditional on declared feature classes; Ce's acid slope is ambiguous (M28).
idea.test_design: (1) Crossed random-effects (or relation-class moment) model of B1 hidden-level deviations, scored only through pair contrasts, metal-specific variances, Student-t errors; cluster_cpg bootstrap (2,000) and publication bootstrap; map to T, L, I shares. (2) Dose-response a + b/n on all cells with >= 2 siblings (subsets up to n = 6, <= 50 per n), per pair type, families weighted equally, family bootstrap; condition-aware within-family ridge arm (per-metal log D on log acid and log L, shrunk to family mean) to test whether a is reducible; placebo with random other-family siblings. (3) Validation: the budget must reproduce publication offsets 0.476-0.533, chemotype-from-other-publications about +0.006, kernel BLUP 0.564 (M03) and the 15-cell replicate share. Freeze the futility rule before fitting; report with and without C5-BTBP and the giant cluster.
idea.kill_criterion: Decision rule: upper 95 % bound of T < 8.8 % of SSE registers futility for model-only routes to 0.50 under BPG (budget moves to known-lab regimes, more reads, measurement and provenance); lower bound >= 4.4 % justifies one powered model slot; otherwise inconclusive. Headroom remains (idea killed) if a/B1 MSE < 0.40 with interval excluding 0.5, or the condition-aware arm lowers a by >= 30 %, or extrapolated cross-source headroom > +0.05 with lower bound > +0.01. Budget invalid if it fails >= 2 of the 4 validation cross-fits.
idea.expected_effect: T about 1-4 % (upper 5-9 %); L about 15-30 %; I about 45-60 %; cross-source headroom above B1 about +0.02 to +0.06.
idea.practical_value: Decides whether to stop asking cross-source or structure models for adjacent SF from 4 metals and invest in reference series, extra reads or data quality. Without own-lab data, pair-level error below about 0.13 log should not be expected. Gives a software prior for the repeatability campaign (M11).
idea.risks: Crossed models unstable on heavy-tailed unbalanced data (moment fallback); futility must be phrased as conditional on a seen corpus; lab identity approximated by publication; a only bounds noise from above.
idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: statistics-5, contrarian-1; first joint budget with an interval for the transferable share, a sibling-count dose-response ceiling, and a pre-registered futility rule.

idea.title: Screening estimand for ranking candidates from partial series, with a slope-only LINE control

idea.title: Publication vs cluster confirmation units: calibrated simulation using the measured within-cluster publication ICC
idea.lens: evaluation and inference design (H-UNIT)
idea.hypothesis: A publication-level confirmation test (sign test or IM-t over publications, optionally chemotype-stratified) keeps size <= 0.075 only when publication gains are not too strongly shared within clusters; at the measured ICC this holds only with chemotype stratification or independent-lab layouts. idea.rationale: Publication Kish 18.8 vs cluster Kish 2.24 is the difference between a feasible and an infeasible confirmation, and validity depends on how strongly gains are shared across publications of the same chemistry, which can be measured on the development corpus and carried into a simulation.

Probit toy on the real layout: publication sign test size 0.027 under independence, 0.064 / 0.104 / 0.137 / 0.198 at latent rho 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.3 / 0.5. B1 - B0's 31/38 stays significant even at rho 0.5 (0.019). Cross-publication same-extractant residual correlation 0.10-0.14.

Tests: publication sign test, publication IM-t, chemotype-stratified publication permutation, cluster sign-flip, cluster IM-t, sealed rule. idea.title: E-CENS: two-sided interval scoring at measurement limits, a label-rule sensitivity that re-levels R2 without re-ranking arms

idea.title: Nested data-version ladder (V1 | E-CENS | V2-S | V2 | V3) with a fragility flag, plus closure of robust-loss routes
idea.lens: data quality and evaluation robustness
idea.hypothesis: Round-5 conclusions can be made robust to contested data without editing V1: every contrast is reported on a fixed ladder of rule-sourced data versions, and a candidate whose sign vs B1 flips on any source-evidence rung is data-fragile and cannot be a finalist. Robust (Huber/LAD) losses add nothing and should not take a slot.

Nested, pre-declared rungs separate them and answer 'is this about the data or the model?' for every contrast.

Freeze rung definitions with digests and rule sources: V1 (none); E-CENS (scoring rule, M23); V2-S (documented defects with source or archive evidence); V2 (V2-S + value-pattern V2-5); V3 (blind source recovery, M25). 2. On each rung refit B0, B1 (fold beta) and HIST_D7, rebuild DOPT_Q sets with that rung's training covariance, and score every round-5 candidate under BPG (BP sensitivity) with cluster_cpg intervals; reproduction checks per rung (B0 to 1e-12 where data are unchanged). 3. One table of dSSE vs B1 per rung plus provenance-class columns (M21). 4. Fragility flag: sign differs between V1 and V2-S or V3, or the cluster interval moves from excluding to including 0. 5. Decisions use E-A on V1 only; flagged candidates cannot be finalists. 6. Huber re-scoring and Huber beta as one diagnostic line.

idea.title: Sequential confirmation ledger valid at any stopping point: an e-process on 'beats B1 on a new independent source', with a magnitude guard
idea.lens: evaluation and inference design (anytime-valid sequential testing)
idea.hypothesis: Freezing one finalist and running an e-process on per-source win indicators (or bounded per-source relative SSE) keeps type-I error <= 0.05 under optional stopping and across rounds, and reaches 70-90 % power for a B1-like consistent gain within 20-30 new sources, which realistic supply can reach over several rounds; the fixed-G sealed rule never can.
idea.rationale: Supply arrives in trickles (0-2 repository and 3-5 literature sources per round), while the sealed rule needs one batch of 40-80 and spends alpha at every look. Test martingales allow adding sources one at a time and stopping early for success or futility, and the per-source estimand is what a user cares about.
idea.evidence_for: Fixed-bet e-process (lambda 0.6, reject at E >= 20), 20,000 runs: size 0.007-0.035 at pi = 0.5 for G = 8-40. Power at pi = 0.8: 0.21 / 0.40 / 0.54 / 0.73 / 0.91 at G = 8 / 10 / 15 / 20 / 30, vs fixed sign test 0.38 (G 10) / 0.80 (G 20) and sealed rule 0.14 at G = 20; median stop 7-13 sources. idea.test_design: 1. Register estimand pi = P(candidate SSE < B1 SSE on a new independent source's strict-adjacent queries at k = 3, DOPT_Q), with guards: running pooled relative SSE >= 0 and a betting e-process on per-source relative SSE bounded to [-1, 1]. 2. Freeze one finalist per claim and record its code hash. 3. Score each arriving source once on arrival, append with provenance and date; merge same-cluster sources into one unit (rule from M36). 4. Stop for success at E >= 20; for futility when the 95 % confidence-sequence upper bound on pi < 0.65; never reset. 5. Before use, simulate with the M36 generator under an arrival schedule of 3-7 sources per round for pi in {0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9} and the heterogeneous zero-mean null (>= 200 replicates).
idea.kill_criterion: Abandoned if, in the calibrated generator, a B1-like effect (delta 0.034, tau 0.065) has pi <= 0.65, or the e-process size exceeds 0.05 in any null world. idea.lens: measurement design (condition choice, detection-floor-aware design)
idea.hypothesis: The tail of adjacent-SF irreproducibility sits where log D < about -3 (and partly > 2), mainly for light pairs. idea.rationale: Out-of-window rows hold about half of B1's SSE, and adjacent log SF is largely condition-invariant within a lab, so sibling disagreement measures how reliable a measured SF is at each level. This converts the error anatomy into a measurement instruction rather than a modelling target.
idea.evidence_for: Sibling pairs (6,066 pair-rows, 20 publications): rms dSF 0.172 with all values in [-2, 2], 0.224 with any > 2, 0.329 with any < -2; by mean level <= -3 0.485, (-3, -2] 0.100; light pairs in vs out: Ce/Pr 0.193 vs 0.757, Sm/Eu 0.204 vs 0.398; heavy pairs unchanged; 7/11 publications out > in. Within-series roughness: robust sd 0.049 in vs 0.085 out, rms 0.110 vs 0.203 (0.302 at min <= -3); out > in in 15/20 extractant x publication groups (sign p 0.021); robust sd of condition-to-condition differences similar in and out, so the window adds outliers, not width. Reads-only flags: all reads in [-2, 2] 0.500 on 62 %; min read >= -2 0.500 on 83.5 %.
idea.evidence_against: Effect is in the tail only, and the (-3, -2] band is the most consistent; confounded with publication (C5-BTBP supplies 986 out-of-window rows) and with extreme conditions where SF may truly change (loading, aggregation); no effect on heavy pairs; thresholds seen post hoc; the window depends on phase ratio and analytical method.
idea.test_design: (a) Registered sibling-consistency analysis: within publication x extractant x pair type compare |dSF| for siblings with all values in [-3, 2], any < -3, any > 2; stratified permutation test (labels permuted within publication x pair type), publication-level sign test, trimmed and untrimmed rms; sensitivity without C5-BTBP. (b) Reads-only flags on the pre-declared grid L in {-3, -2.5, -2} x U in {2, 2.5, 3}: coverage-R2 for B0 and B1 against stratified random abstention at equal coverage (as in M09), per-cluster coverage, BPG deciding. (c) Supply the low-D arm of the repeatability campaign (M11).
idea.kill_criterion: (a) Killed if the stratified permutation p > 0.05 for rms(< -3) > rms(in window), or fewer than 60 % of qualifying publications show out > in. (b) Killed if no pre-declared reads-only window beats random abstention by >= 0.03 R2 at >= 70 % coverage.
idea.expected_effect: rms dSF ratio below -3 vs in window 1.5-2.5 (light pairs 2-4); reads-only window R2 0.50-0.54 at 60-85 % coverage vs about 0.45 random.
idea.practical_value: Before relying on or reporting adjacent SF, adjust extractant concentration or acidity so the metals of interest have log D between about -3 and +2; process designers operate near log D 0 anyway. If any of the 4 reads is below -3, treat predicted light-pair SFs as unreliable.
idea.risks: Window effects could be real chemistry; publication confounding with 20 publications; threshold selection; overlap with M09 (the new part is the measurement evidence and the condition-choice rule).
idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: measurement-5 (plus the within-series roughness check from acquisition-2); sibling consistency used as a replicate proxy, the tail-not-width finding, and a condition-choice rule.

idea.title: Value of the next measurement across a screening set: allocate extra reads between cells, not between metals
idea.lens: measurement design (adaptive budget allocation across candidates)
idea.hypothesis: The SSE reduction from a 5th read is predictable between cells from label-free read features, even though it is not within a cell. Allocating half the extra reads to cells with the largest predicted adjacent-SF mass (sum of |B1 predicted log SF|) captures most of the full-budget gain and beats random and size-only allocation.
idea.rationale: B1's error concentrates in cells with a wide spread of SFs (Spearman of cell MSE with cell sd of y 0.91). A screening campaign or literature gap-filling spends its budget across extractants, so the useful question is which extractant gets the next measurement, not which metal (the latter is nearly unlearnable).
idea.evidence_for: Spearman(score, SSE drop): predicted-SF mass 0.55 (DOPT_Q-nested) / 0.60 (max-min); read range x hidden count 0.51 / 0.58; size only 0.44 / 0.42. Max-min 5th read on 50 % of eligible cells: score 0.4914, random 0.4771, size-only 0.4850, oracle 0.5027, all cells 0.5030 (from 0.4511), so half the reads deliver 78 % of the gain; score - random +0.014 [+0.002, +0.031], LOCO [+0.007, +0.019]; score - size +0.006 [-0.004, +0.033]. DOPT_Q-nested: 0.4819 vs 0.4734 vs oracle 0.4956.
idea.evidence_against: Score picked among 9 tried; most of the gain is cell size (+0.008 of +0.014) and the spread part over size has an interval including 0; fixed beta; large-|SF| cells are also where tail noise lives; moot with ICP-MS where all metals come together.
idea.test_design: Registered E-G, no training. Primary score: sum over adjacent pairs of |B1 predicted log SF| at k = 3 (B1 fold refit); secondary read range x hidden count. Budgets {0.25, 0.5} of eligible cells. Next read DOPT_Q-nested (primary) and max-min (secondary). Arms: score, size-only, random (exact expectation), oracle allocation. Endpoint pooled R2 at fixed total reads with balanced MAE guard; BPG decides; cluster bootstrap and LOCO; with and without C5-BTBP.
idea.kill_criterion: Killed at the 50 % budget under BPG with B1 refit if score - random < +0.005 R2, or score <= size-only + 0.002, or the score - random cluster lower bound <= 0.
idea.expected_effect: At 50 % budget: +0.008 to +0.015 over random, +0.003 to +0.006 over size-only.
idea.practical_value: When screening 10-30 extractants where each extra metal costs a separate determination or literature search: after 4 metals each, spend the next measurement on extractants with the largest predicted adjacent SFs; half the extra measurements give about 80 % of the benefit.
idea.risks: Partly 'measure the big cells' (size-only control must be shown); large-SF floor cells may make the gain partly noise; only one pre-declared score.
idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: measurement-4; between-cell allocation and its exchange rate with random and size-only allocation were never evaluated (only within-cell adaptive choice).

idea.title: Unmeasurable-end scenario: predict the two adjacent SFs of a metal that cannot be measured, from its measured neighbours
idea.lens: measurement design (pair-targeted reads, the stated scenario for gap G8)
idea.hypothesis: When a laboratory cannot measure one metal but measures both its Z-neighbours, radius interpolation predicts that metal's two adjacent SFs with the accuracy of the bench's isolated-hidden-metal analogues (R2 about 0.55, MAE about 0.11 log, direction about 0.8). External series in which that metal was measured decide between plain radius interpolation and a tetrad-boundary kink.
idea.rationale: Pair-targeted reads win 12/12 pair types, but a lab able to read one end can usually read the other, so G8 asks for a scenario where one end cannot be measured. A metal without a stable isotope, bracketed by two routinely measured neighbours, is that scenario and the cleanest geometry available.
idea.evidence_for: Bench proxy (middle metal predicted from both neighbours, all V1 cells): hidden Pr R2 0.542, MAE 0.114, direction 0.843 (0.898 for |y| >= 0.1); hidden Eu 0.559 / 0.111 / 0.794; Dy 0.692; Ho 0.556; Tm 0.462; Er 0.287. Per-metal table split-half reliability 0.79 [0.55, 0.94]. Isolated hidden metals with a 2-Z bracket give 0.539 (E2).
idea.evidence_against: The archive has essentially no data for the motivating metal, so validation depends on external series, which are mostly acidic organophosphorus systems while C3 is mostly DGA; the metal sits at a tetrad boundary (the Nd dip shows the neighbour chord is chemistry-dependent); external data come from a different measurement technique with different noise.
idea.test_design: (a) Bench, training-free, registered: an 'unmeasurable middle metal' estimand for every interior metal, scored on its two adjacent SFs; arms radius interpolation, Z interpolation and a pre-declared tetrad-kink variant; chemotype and cluster bootstrap; Gd handled with B1's term. (b) Desk validation (web reading only, no downloads; closed papers need the user): pre-register extraction rules and scoring before reading values; compile series with the target metal and both neighbours under one condition (target >= 8 series from >= 4 labs); report MAE, direction and the sign of the deviation from the neighbour chord (tests the tetrad reading, C8).
idea.kill_criterion: (a) Killed if the light-analogue (Pr, Eu) proxy R2 has a cluster lower bound < 0.40 or direction accuracy < 0.75. (b) Killed (proxy only, not offered to users) if the median |error| of the predicted level exceeds the median |adjacent SF|, or fewer than 4 independent external series exist.
idea.expected_effect: Proxy R2 0.50-0.56, direction about 0.8; 3-8 external series; a systematic deviation would favour the tetrad reading of the Nd dip.
idea.practical_value: Lets a chemist estimate selectivity involving a metal they cannot handle from cold measurements of its neighbours, and gives the programme the concrete one-end-unmeasurable scenario G8 asked for.
idea.risks: The proxy is not the target metal; small chemotype-skewed validation set; figure-read values carry transcription noise.
idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: measurement-7; the isolated-middle accuracy table with reliability, a stated unmeasurable-end scenario, and an external test that also bears on the Nd-dip origin.

idea.title: Yttrium as a 4f-free internal probe: Y's offset from the Ln radius curve as a label-free index of non-radius chemistry
idea.lens: physics and chemistry (Y has no 4f electrons, radius near Ho) + new data acquisition
idea.hypothesis: Y_dev = log D(Y) - PWL_R of the measured Ln evaluated at Y's radius (CN8 about 1.019 A, between Dy and Ho) measures how far a system departs from pure size selectivity. |Y_dev| correlates with the cell's |Gd dip| and roughness (partial rho >= 0.3 controlling for slope) and flags cells where B1 fails; a Y-calibrated Gd amplitude (beta0 + kappa*Y_dev) could transfer the extractant-specific dip that no structural descriptor has transferred.
idea.rationale: The Gd dip is extractant-specific (ICC 0.69), condition-invariant within an extractant and additive (not amplitude-scaled), so what is missing is a cheap per-cell non-amplitude handle. Y is present in every heavy-REE feed, is routinely measured by ICP-MS at no extra cost, and its known extractant-dependent position along the Ln series suggests a large, chemistry-specific signal.
idea.evidence_for: The archive has 49 Y rows from 4 DOIs, one extractant family; at the 3 conditions with bracketing Ln reads Y_dev is -0.27, -0.26 and -0.01, the same order as the Gd dip. Literature: Y's pseudo-position moves from the Ce-Pr region to Ho-Er across carboxylic-acid extractants and sits among the middle Ln for a neutral organophosphorus extractant; Y/Ho fractionation is a geochemical non-radius tracer.
idea.evidence_against: Untestable now (3 usable conditions); Y differs from Ln in mass and possibly hydration, so Y_dev may carry a universal offset unrelated to covalency; Y's radius depends on coordination number; Y is often absent from new sources; a Y-calibrated term needs a Y read in every deployment.
idea.test_design: Request Y in every acquisition (M05, M11, M31, M32, M33) and digitise it from open sources. Freeze the definition before any value arrives: PWL_R through the measured Ln at the CN8 radius of Y (CN9 as sensitivity); an all-Ln version (diagnostic) and a read-only version from the k = 3 DOPT_Q reads (deployable). Endpoints on >= 20 cells from >= 8 extractant units (>= 5 laboratories): partial Spearman(|Y_dev|, |Gd dip|), (|Y_dev|, cell roughness) and (|Y_dev_reads|, cell B1 MSE), each controlling for |slope|, with unit bootstrap; permutation of Y_dev across units within donor class as control. Model arms: B1-Y (Gd beta = beta0 + kappa*Y_dev, kappa fitted leave-one-laboratory-out) on Eu/Gd and Gd/Tb; B1+Y (Y as an extra read at its radius) on Dy/Ho and Ho/Er, paired per-unit sign.
idea.kill_criterion: With >= 20 cells from >= 8 units: killed if every partial |rho| < 0.3 or every bootstrap CI includes 0, or B1-Y does not reduce Eu/Gd + Gd/Tb SSE by >= 10 % leave-one-laboratory-out, or B1+Y loses to B1 on > 50 % of units for the Ho-region pairs. Y is then recorded for Y/Ln separation use only.
idea.expected_effect: Unknown (data-gated); a partial rho of about 0.3-0.5 if the dip is covalency-driven; any gain confined to Gd-region and Ho-region pairs.
idea.practical_value: Y/Ho and Y/Dy are core industrial separations and B1 makes no Y prediction today; if Y_dev tracks non-radius behaviour, one extra free analyte warns a chemist that 4-metal interpolation will be unreliable for that extractant and places Y on the curve.
idea.risks: Requested data may never arrive from enough independent labs; Y_dev may be a universal offset; the radius convention must be fixed in advance.
idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: physics-6, acquisition-8; an operational Y_dev estimand (all-Ln and read-only versions), first archive values, slope-controlled thresholds, a permutation control and two scored model arms.

idea.title: Rigid and preorganised chemotype stress set: how many metals are needed when the series has an interior extremum
idea.lens: new data acquisition (rigid/preorganised chemotypes) + k ladder
idea.hypothesis: For rigid or preorganised extractants whose series have an interior extremum, B1 with 4 DOPT_Q reads falls well below its C3 level (R2 < 0.30), and reaching 0.50 needs at least 2 more measured metals than monotone chemistry, or an extremum-aware read rule.
idea.rationale: Radius interpolation cannot represent an interior extremum it did not read, and the strongest such shapes come from chemotypes almost absent from C3 (157/229 cells DGA). A user evaluating a new rigid ligand needs a metal-count rule the corpus cannot give.
idea.evidence_for: 14 C3 cells (about 9 % of rows) have a smoothed interior extremum >= 0.3 log beyond both ends: B1 0.316 (B0 0.300), MSE 0.064, vs 0.468 and 0.024 on 182 monotone-like cells; B1's Gd gain there only +0.016 (label-based classification, descriptive only). gen15: 27 % of well-determined cells have an interior extremum; a shape oracle is worth +0.056 but is not predictable from the 2D graph. Literature reports V-shaped curves for phenanthroline diamides. C6 ladder 0.385 / 0.431 / 0.483 / 0.524 / 0.552 at k = 2-6; per-cell placement oracle 0.632 at k = 3.

idea.test_design: Acquire >= 8 full series (>= 12 Ln, values in [-3, 3]) of rigid or preorganised extractants from >= 4 laboratories (open access plus lab or SAFE series). 'Rigid' defined before any value is seen by a fixed SMARTS list of preorganised scaffolds. Freeze B0/B1 with corpus parameters; read policies DOPT_Q (primary), BISECT and ADAPT_KINK (secondary); k = 1-6 ladder on identical strict-adjacent pairs. Statistics: pooled R2 per k, first k with R2 >= 0.50, per-pair R2 for pairs bracketing the extremum, per-laboratory reporting. Control: the same ladder on >= 8 newly acquired monotone non-DGA series (from M05, M31, M33), separating 'new source' from 'shape' effects.
idea.kill_criterion: Killed (no chemotype-specific rule needed) if B1 at k = 3 on the rigid set reaches >= 0.40 and the first k reaching 0.50 is within 1 read of the monotone control. Supported if B1 at k = 3 < 0.30 and the rigid set needs >= 2 more reads than the control.
idea.expected_effect: About 0.3 at k = 3; a likely rule 'for preorganised N-donors measure >= 7 metals including both neighbours of the expected extremum'.
idea.practical_value: A measured minimum metal count, and where to place the reads, for a chemist who has just made a rigid size-selective ligand, which are the ligands most likely to give unusual adjacent selectivity.
idea.risks: Small n and family clustering; plotted values need double digitisation (M22).
idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: acquisition-7; a descriptive penalty for extremum cells in C3, a frozen k ladder with a monotone new-data control, and a decision rule phrased as a metal count.

idea.title: Provenance class (figure-digitised / table / no location) as a frozen, label-free reporting axis
idea.lens: data quality and provenance (reporting stratum)
idea.hypothesis: The archive's data_location class is label-free metadata that strongly modifies B1's difficulty and its Gd gain: figure-digitised series are smoother with a weaker Gd dip, and B1's gain lives almost entirely in table and no-location cells, so the pooled 0.452 averages three different benchmarks.

NONE: 80 cells, 12 of 13 clusters, 59.5 % of SSE, holds 2.29 of B1's 3.02 SSE/seed gain. Within sc009: B1 - B0 -0.015 FIG / +0.030 TAB / +0.056 NONE; median |second difference| 0.038 / 0.065 / 0.074; fitted Gd amplitude -0.040 / -0.116 / -0.163. For B0, B1 and every round-5 candidate on V1 C3 k = 3 DOPT_Q, BPG deciding, report per class: R2, dSSE % vs B1, B1 - B0, cluster counts. 3. Lead sub-test (exploratory): within sc009, FIG - TAB difference in per-row B1 - B0 dSSE, publication bootstrap (15 publications, 2,000 draws) and a permutation of class labels among whole publications (1,000). 4. Within-publication check on the 3 publications with both FIG and TAB cells and the 12 two-location cells. Class-conditional models forbidden unless pre-registered with a power study.

idea.title: B1+ as a pre-specified 2 x 2 factorial: Ce log-acid offset x damped heavy-end continuation, with a fold-starvation diagnosis
idea.lens: statistical modelling of the residual (scalar metal-local terms, cross-fitting with one-SE selection)
idea.hypothesis: Two one-dimensional, pre-specified terms each improve B1 under leave-one-cluster-out and are additive because they touch disjoint rows: (a) an additive offset to the hidden Ce level, linear in log10 acid and fitted with a Huber loss; (b) a damped continuation of the last read slope beyond the heaviest read. Under BPG their gain is attenuated mainly by fold starvation (the big fold trains on 51-69 cells).
idea.rationale: Ce pairs carry 34.2 % of B1's SSE and the 12 % of rows beyond the read hull have R2 about 0. Both are metal-local with one physically motivated degree of freedom, and scalar terms are the only kind of correction that has survived cross-fitting. A factorial tests both terms and their interaction in one slot and defines an honest 'B1+' reference. It is the positive counterpart of M27's Ce null.
idea.evidence_for: Ce hidden-level error (sd 0.239) Spearman with log acid -0.20 (685 cell-seeds) and -0.33 on the bench; within publication -0.23 (82 cells, 13 publications; per-publication median -0.31, 5 of 7 negative); slope about -0.09 to -0.10 per decade. Leave-one-cluster-out: +0.0094 (OLS) / +0.0101 (Huber); Ce pairs 0.399 -> 0.43; intercept-only control -0.001, so the gain is the slope. Edge: leave-cluster-out +0.0051 to +0.0055; half-slope +0.0047; rows disjoint from Ce rows. Read-spike shrinkage and level-dependent shrinkage toward 0 lose (-0.004 / -0.029 / -0.003).
idea.evidence_against: Under BPG folds the Ce term gives only +0.0014 / +0.0024 with fitted slopes from -0.113 to +0.017; a within-publication fixed-effects slope variant loses (-0.007 / -0.017); acid slopes for all metals are destructive (R2 0.27 / 0.34); the La-level gate is between-publication only; M27 finds Ce correlations vanish within publication on the bench (-0.11); the edge term is <= +0.0055 everywhere; the combined effect is likely below the 0.01 margin under BPG.
idea.test_design: Factorial {B1, +Ce, +edge, +Ce+edge} on identical rows (V1 C3, k = 3, DOPT_Q) under BPG (deciding), BP and leave-one-cluster-out (13 folds). Ce term: delta_Ce = a + b*log10(clip(acid, 0.01, 10)), Huber loss, fitted on training cells where Ce is hidden using B1's level error under each training cell's own read set; applied only when Ce is hidden. Edge term: continuation slope d*s_last beyond the heaviest read, d fitted on training folds. Each term switched on or off by inner leave-cluster-out SSE with a one-SE rule toward off; report the inner-outer gap per fold. Controls: acid values permuted within publication (Ce); end slope drawn from another training cell with the same read geometry (edge). Outcomes: pooled R2, cluster-balanced log SSE ratio with sign-flip test (M34), La/Ce + Ce/Pr and extrapolated-row R2, all per fold type (big fold vs rest) to test starvation directly.
idea.kill_criterion: Ce term killed if < +0.003 pooled R2 under BPG and < +0.005 under leave-cluster-out, or if the within-publication acid permutation keeps >= 50 % of its gain. Edge term killed if < +0.003 on both designs. Fold-starvation explanation rejected if the Ce gain outside the big fold is not larger than inside it.
idea.expected_effect: BPG +0.004 to +0.008 combined; leave-cluster-out +0.010 to +0.016; La/Ce + Ce/Pr subgroup +0.02 to +0.04.
idea.practical_value: Defines the honest reference for every later contrast. If the Ce term survives: at low acidity Ce is extracted about 0.09 log per decade of acid more than the La-Pr chord implies, so La/Ce or Ce/Pr targets at low acid need a Ce measurement. The edge term stops the reference from predicting SF = 1 for heavy pairs beyond the last measured metal.
idea.risks: Ce-acid may be confounded with publication (floor cells, specific labs); slope instability in the starved big fold; gains below the margin are still informative as a reference but not as a claim.
idea.novelty_vs_previous: sources: statistics-6; the factorial, the single-metal restriction justified by the destructive all-metal result, the fold-starvation test, and the negative results for spike and level shrinkage; run jointly with M27, which reaches the opposite conclusion on Ce.
